title.zh: 卷三百六十四 列傳第一百二十三 韓世忠
title.raw: 卷三百六十四 列傳第一百二十三 韓世忠 Volume 364 Biographies 123: Han Shizhong

sentences.zh: 韓世忠子:彥直

translations.literal: Han Shizhong's son: Yan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong's son: Yan Zhi

sentences.zh: 韓世忠

translations.literal: Han Shizhong
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong

sentences.zh: 韓世忠，字良臣，延安人。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong, style name Liangchen, was a native of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong, whose style name was Liangchen, came from Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 風骨偉岸，目瞬如電。

translations.literal: His bearing was imposing and his gaze flashed like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: He had a towering presence, and his eyes flashed like lightning.

sentences.zh: 早年鷙勇絕人，能騎生馬駒。

translations.literal: In his youth he was fierce and brave beyond others, and could ride unbroken colts.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was ferociously brave beyond compare and could ride unbroken foals.

sentences.zh: 家貧無產業，嗜酒尚氣，不可繩檢。

translations.literal: His family was poor and without property; he loved wine and prized honor, and could not be restrained by rules.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and owned no property; he loved wine and prized his honor, and no discipline could hold him in check.

sentences.zh: 日者言當作三公，世忠怒其侮己，毆之。

translations.literal: A diviner said he would attain the rank of the Three Excellencies; Shizhong, angry that he was being insulted, beat him.
translations.idiomatic: When a fortune-teller said he was destined for the Three Excellencies, Shizhong, enraged at what he took as mockery, beat the man.

sentences.zh: 年十八，以敢勇應募鄉州，隸赤籍，挽強馳射，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: At eighteen he enlisted in his district for his daring bravery, was entered on the red register, drew the strong bow and rode shooting, and his courage topped the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he enlisted in his home district for his daring, was entered on the military register, excelled at drawing the heavy bow and shooting from horseback, and was the bravest man in the army.

sentences.zh: 崇寧四年，西夏騷動，郡調兵捍禦，世忠在遣中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning, the Western Xia stirred up trouble; the commandery mobilized troops to defend, and Shizhong was among those sent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chongning reign, when the Western Xia rose in revolt, the commandery mobilized troops for defense, and Shizhong was among those dispatched.

sentences.zh: 至銀州，夏人嬰城自固，世忠斬關殺敵將，擲首陴外，諸軍乘之，夏人大敗。

translations.literal: When they reached Yin Prefecture, the Xia people held the city fast in defense; Shizhong cut through the gate and killed an enemy general, threw his head outside the parapet, the armies pressed the advantage, and the Xia suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Yin Prefecture the Xia defenders held the city in a stubborn defense; Shizhong broke through the gate, killed an enemy general, and hurled his head over the wall. The Song forces pressed the attack and routed the Xia army.

sentences.zh: 既而以重兵次蒿平嶺，世忠率精銳鏖戰，解去。

translations.literal: Afterward the enemy massed heavy forces at Haoping Ridge; Shizhong led elite troops in fierce battle and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the enemy concentrated a large force at Haoping Ridge; Shizhong led crack troops in a bitter fight and then broke off.

sentences.zh: 俄復出間道，世忠獨部敢死士珠死鬥，敵少卻，顧一騎士銳甚，問俘者，曰：「監軍駙馬兀𠼪也。

translations.literal: Soon they again came out by a hidden path; Shizhong alone led dare-to-die troops in desperate fighting, the enemy fell back slightly, and seeing one very sharp rider he asked a captive, who said: "It is the supervising army's imperial son-in-law Wuzha."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy reappeared by a side road; Shizhong alone led a band of dare-to-die men in a fight to the death. The enemy gave ground slightly, and when he noticed an especially fierce rider he asked a prisoner, who said, "That is Wuzha, the supervising army's imperial son-in-law."

sentences.zh: 」躍馬斬之，敵眾大潰。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse forward and cut him down, and the enemy masses broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse forward and cut the man down, and the enemy host collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 經略司上其功，童貫董邊事，疑有所增飾，止補一資，眾弗平。

translations.literal: The frontier commissionerate reported his merit; Tong Guan oversaw border affairs, suspected embellishment, and only granted one step in rank, to the discontent of all.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier commissionerate reported his achievements, but Tong Guan, who directed border affairs, suspected exaggeration and granted only a single step in rank, to widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 從劉延慶築天降山砦，為敵所據，世忠夜登城斬二級，割護城氈以獻。

translations.literal: Following Liu Yanqing he built the Tianjiang Mountain stockade, which the enemy seized; Shizhong climbed the wall by night, cut off two heads, and cut the protective felt from the wall to present.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Yanqing in building the Tianjiang Mountain stockade, which the enemy then seized; Shizhong climbed the wall by night, beheaded two men, and cut away the protective felt matting from the ramparts to present as proof.

sentences.zh: 繼遇敵佛口砦，又斬數級，始補進義副尉。

translations.literal: He next met the enemy at the Fokou stockade, again cut off several heads, and only then was appointed Assistant Commandant for Advancing Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He next fought the enemy at the Fokou stockade, beheaded several more men, and was at last appointed Assistant Commandant for Advancing Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 至藏底河，斬三級，轉進勇副尉。

translations.literal: At the Zangdi River he cut off three heads and was transferred to Assistant Commandant for Advancing Courage.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zangdi River he beheaded three men and was promoted to Assistant Commandant for Advancing Courage.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，方臘反、江、浙震動，調兵四方，世忠以偏將從王淵討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, Fang La rebelled and Jiangsu and Zhejiang were shaken; troops were mobilized from all directions, and Shizhong as a subordinate general followed Wang Yuan to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xuanhe reign, Fang La rebelled and Jiangsu and Zhejiang were thrown into turmoil. Troops were called up from all quarters, and Shizhong served as a subordinate general under Wang Yuan in the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 次杭州，賊奄至，勢張甚，大將惶怖無策。

translations.literal: When they halted at Hangzhou, the rebels suddenly arrived, their momentum very strong, and the chief general was fearful and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Hangzhou, the rebels swept in with overwhelming force, and the commanding general was terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 世忠以兵二千伏北關堰，賊過，伏發，眾蹂亂，世忠追擊，賊敗而遁。

translations.literal: Shizhong with two thousand men lay in ambush at the Beiguan weir; when the rebels passed, the ambush struck, the masses were trampled into disorder, Shizhong pursued, and the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong posted two thousand men in ambush at the Beiguan weir. When the rebels passed, the ambush sprang up, throwing them into chaos; Shizhong pursued, and the rebels were beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 淵歎曰：「真萬人敵也。

translations.literal: Yuan sighed and said: "Truly a match for ten thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan exclaimed, "This man is truly a match for ten thousand."

sentences.zh: 」盡以所隨白金器賞之，且與定交。

translations.literal: He gave him all the white-gold vessels he had with him as reward, and moreover formed a bond of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with all the white-gold vessels he had brought and sealed a bond of friendship with him.

sentences.zh: 時有詔能得臘首者，授兩鎮節鉞。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict that whoever could obtain Fang La's head would be granted the seals of two military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had been issued promising the seals of two military commissions to whoever could capture Fang La.

sentences.zh: 世忠窮追至睦州清溪峒，賊深據岩屋為三窟，諸將繼至，莫知所入。

translations.literal: Shizhong pursued to the end to the Qingxi ravine in Muzhou; the rebels held deep in cliff dwellings with three lairs, the generals arrived in succession, and none knew how to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong pursued relentlessly to the Qingxi ravine in Muzhou, where the rebels held three cliffside lairs in the depths of the mountains. The other generals arrived in turn but none knew how to get in.

sentences.zh: 世忠潛行溪穀，問野婦得徑，即挺身仗戈直前，渡險數里，搗其穴，格殺數十人，禽臘以出。

translations.literal: Shizhong secretly went along stream valleys, asked a country woman and obtained a path, then straightway bore himself forward with spear in hand, crossed several li of peril, stormed their lair, killed several tens in combat, and captured La and brought him out.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong stole along the stream valleys, asked a peasant woman for the path, then strode forward spear in hand, crossed several li of treacherous ground, stormed their lair, killed dozens in hand-to-hand fighting, and captured Fang La alive.

sentences.zh: 辛興宗領兵截峒口，掠其俘為己功，故賞不及世忠。

translations.literal: Xin Xingzong led troops to block the ravine mouth, seized his captives as his own merit, and therefore rewards did not reach Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xingzong led troops to block the ravine mouth and claimed Shizhong's prisoners as his own achievement, so the rewards never reached Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 別帥楊惟忠還闕，直其事，轉承節郎。

translations.literal: The separate commander Yang Weizhong returned to court, reported the matter truthfully, and he was transferred to Gentleman for Upholding Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Yang Weizhong returned to court and reported what had really happened, and Shizhong was promoted to Gentleman for Upholding Integrity.

sentences.zh: 三年，議復燕山，調諸軍，至則皆潰。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the recovery of Yanshan was debated, the armies were mobilized, but on arrival all collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the court debated recovering Yanshan, armies were mobilized, but on arrival they all broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 世忠往見劉延慶，與蘇格等五十騎俱抵滹沱河。

translations.literal: Shizhong went to see Liu Yanqing, and with Su Ge and fifty riders together reached the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong went to join Liu Yanqing and, with Su Ge and fifty horsemen, reached the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 逢金兵二千餘騎，格失措，世忠從容令格等列高岡，戒勿動。

translations.literal: They met more than two thousand Jin horsemen; Ge was at a loss, but Shizhong calmly ordered Ge and the others to form on the high ridge and warned them not to move.
translations.idiomatic: They encountered more than two thousand Jin horsemen. Su Ge panicked, but Shizhong calmly ordered him and the others to form up on a high ridge and warned them not to stir.

sentences.zh: 屬燕山潰卒舟集，即命艤河岸，約鼓噪助聲勢。

translations.literal: Just then boats of routed soldiers from Yanshan gathered, and he immediately ordered them to moor along the bank and agreed they would beat drums and shout to augment the show of force.
translations.idiomatic: Just then boats carrying routed soldiers from Yanshan gathered along the shore; he immediately ordered them to moor and arranged for them to beat drums and shout to swell the apparent force.

sentences.zh: 世忠躍馬薄敵，迴旋如飛。

translations.literal: Shizhong spurred his horse to press the enemy, wheeling like flight.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong spurred his horse against the enemy, wheeling and charging like lightning.

sentences.zh: 敵分二隊據高阜，世忠出其不意，突二執旗者，因奮擊，格等夾攻之，舟卒鼓噪，敵大亂，追斬甚眾。

translations.literal: The enemy split into two bands holding the high mound; Shizhong caught them unawares, burst upon the two flag-bearers, then struck fiercely; Ge and the others attacked from both sides, the boatmen beat drums and shouted, the enemy fell into great disorder, and in pursuit many were cut down.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy split into two bands on the high ground. Shizhong took them by surprise, charged the two standard-bearers, and pressed the attack fiercely while Ge and the others struck from both flanks and the boatmen drummed and shouted. The Jin forces fell into chaos, and many were cut down in the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 時山東、河北盜賊蜂起，世忠從王淵、梁方平討捕，禽戮殆盡，積功轉武節郎。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Shandong and Hebei swarmed up; Shizhong followed Wang Yuan and Liang Fangping in suppression, captured and killed nearly all, and through accumulated merit was transferred to Gentleman for Martial Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere in Shandong and Hebei; Shizhong followed Wang Yuan and Liang Fangping in suppressing them, capturing or killing nearly all, and through accumulated merit was promoted to Gentleman for Martial Integrity.

sentences.zh: 時勝捷軍張師正敗，宣撫副使李彌大斬之，大校李復鼓眾以亂，淄、青之附者合數萬人，山東復擾。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shizheng of the Shengjie Army was defeated; the deputy commissioner Li Yida executed him; the senior officer Li Fu roused the masses to revolt; those attached in Zi and Qing totaled tens of thousands, and Shandong was disturbed again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizheng of the Shengjie Army had been defeated and the deputy frontier commissioner Li Yida executed him, but senior officer Li Fu stirred the troops to mutiny. His followers in Zibo and Qingzhou numbered tens of thousands, and Shandong was thrown into turmoil again.

sentences.zh: 彌大檄世忠將所部追擊，至臨淄河，兵不滿千，分為四隊，布鐵蒺藜自塞歸路，令曰：「進則勝，退則死，走者命後隊剿殺。

translations.literal: Yida issued a dispatch for Shizhong to lead his command in pursuit; at the Linzi River his troops were fewer than a thousand; he divided into four companies, laid iron caltrops to block his own retreat, and ordered: "Advance and you win, retreat and you die; whoever flees, the rear company is ordered to cut him down."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yida ordered Shizhong to lead his troops in pursuit. At the Linzi River he had fewer than a thousand men; he divided them into four companies, laid iron caltrops to block his own retreat, and proclaimed, "Advance and you win; retreat and you die. Anyone who runs, the rear guard is ordered to cut him down."

sentences.zh: 」於是莫敢返顧，皆死戰，大破之，斬復，餘黨奔潰。

translations.literal: Thus none dared look back; all fought to the death, routed them greatly, beheaded Fu, and the remaining partisans fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared look back; they all fought to the death, routed the rebels decisively, beheaded Li Fu, and the rest fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，追至宿遷，賊尚萬人，方擁子女椎牛縱酒。

translations.literal: Pressing victory he pursued north to Suqian; the rebels still numbered ten thousand and were just then embracing wives and children, pounding oxen, and drinking freely.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his victory he pursued north to Suqian, where ten thousand rebels remained, feasting with their families, slaughtering cattle, and drinking freely.

sentences.zh: 世忠單騎夜造其營，呼曰：「大軍至矣，亟束戈卷甲，吾能保全汝，共功名。

translations.literal: Shizhong alone on horseback by night went to their camp and called out: "The great army has arrived; quickly bind up weapons and roll up armor—I can preserve you and share merit together."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong rode alone into their camp by night and called out, "The main army has arrived! Lay down your arms at once—I can spare your lives and share the glory with you."

sentences.zh: 」賊駭粟請命，因跪進牛酒。

translations.literal: The rebels, terrified and trembling, begged for their lives and thereupon knelt to present oxen and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, terrified, begged for mercy and knelt to offer oxen and wine.

sentences.zh: 世忠下馬解鞍，飲啖之盡，於是眾悉就降。

translations.literal: Shizhong dismounted, loosened his saddle, and ate and drank it all up; thus the whole host submitted in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong dismounted, loosened his saddle, and ate and drank with them to the last drop, whereupon the whole band surrendered.

sentences.zh: 黎明，見世忠軍未至，始大悔失色。

translations.literal: At dawn, seeing Shizhong's army had not arrived, they at last deeply regretted it and turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, when they saw that Shizhong's army had never come, they were overcome with regret and turned pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 以功遷左武大夫、果州團練使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Left Martial Grandee and regimental commissioner of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was promoted to Left Martial Grandee and regimental commissioner of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔入朝，授正任單州團練使，屯滹沱河。

translations.literal: He was ordered to enter court, appointed regular regimental commissioner of Shan Prefecture, and stationed at the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court, appointed regular regimental commissioner of Shan Prefecture, and stationed along the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 時真定失守，世忠知王淵守趙，遂亟往。

translations.literal: At that time Zhending was lost; Shizhong knew Wang Yuan was holding Zhao, and therefore hastened there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhending fell, Shizhong learned that Wang Yuan was holding Zhao and hurried to join him.

sentences.zh: 金人至，聞世忠在，攻益急，糧盡援絕。

translations.literal: The Jin came; hearing Shizhong was there, their attacks grew fiercer; grain was exhausted and relief cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin arrived and learned Shizhong was in the city, their assaults grew fiercer. Provisions ran out and reinforcements ceased.

sentences.zh: 人多勉其潰圍去，弗聽。

translations.literal: Many urged him to break out of the encirclement and leave; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Many urged him to break out of the siege and withdraw, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，夜半，以死士三百搗敵營。

translations.literal: It happened to snow heavily; at midnight he sent three hundred dare-to-die men to storm the enemy camp.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy snow fell; at midnight he sent three hundred dare-to-die men to raid the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 敵驚亂，自相擊刺，及旦盡遁。

translations.literal: The enemy were startled into disorder, stabbed one another, and by dawn all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked and turned on one another in the darkness; by dawn they had all fled.

sentences.zh: 後有自金國來者，始知大酋是日被創死，故眾不能支。

translations.literal: Later someone came from the Jin state, and only then was it known that the great chief had been wounded to death that day, and therefore the masses could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Later, refugees from the Jin side revealed that the enemy commander had been mortally wounded that night, which was why his army could not hold.

sentences.zh: 遷嘉州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defender-in-chief of Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defender-in-chief of Jia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還大名，趙野辟為前軍統制。

translations.literal: Returning to Daming, Zhao Ye appointed him commander of the vanguard army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Daming, Zhao Ye appointed him commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 時康王如濟州，世忠領所部勸進。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Kang went to Jizhou; Shizhong led his command to urge his advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang went to Jizhou, Shizhong led his troops to urge him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 金人縱兵逼城，人心忷懼，世忠據西王台力戰，金人少卻。

translations.literal: The Jin released troops to press the city; hearts were fearful and alarmed; Shizhong held the West King Terrace and fought fiercely; the Jin fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed the city with their armies and panic spread among the defenders. Shizhong held the West King Terrace and fought fiercely until the Jin gave ground.

sentences.zh: 翌日，酋帥率眾數萬至，時世忠戲下僅千人，單騎突入，斬其酋長，遂大潰。

translations.literal: The next day the chief led tens of thousands; at that time Shizhong had under him only a thousand men; he alone on horseback burst in, cut down their chieftain, and they thereupon broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an enemy commander arrived with tens of thousands of men. Shizhong had barely a thousand troops under him, but he charged in alone on horseback, cut down the enemy leader, and routed their army.

sentences.zh: 康王即皇帝位，授光州觀察使、帶禦器械。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang assumed the imperial throne; he was appointed observation commissioner of Guang Prefecture and bearer of the imperial armory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang ascended the throne, Shizhong was appointed observation commissioner of Guang Prefecture and bearer of the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 世忠請移都長安，下兵收兩河，時論不從。

translations.literal: Shizhong requested moving the capital to Chang'an and sending troops down to recover the two He provinces; contemporary opinion did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong urged moving the capital to Chang'an and sending armies to recover the two He provinces, but the court would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 初建禦營，為左軍統制。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Camp was first established, he became commander of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Camp was first established, he was made commander of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 是歲，命王淵、張俊討陳州叛兵，劉光世討黎驛叛兵，喬仲福討京東賊李昱，世忠討單州賊魚台。

translations.literal: That year Wang Yuan and Zhang Jun were ordered to suppress the Chenzhou rebels, Liu Guangshi the Liyi rebels, Qiao Zhongfu the Jingdong bandit Li Yu, and Shizhong the Shanzhou bandit Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Yuan and Zhang Jun were ordered against the Chenzhou mutineers, Liu Guangshi against the Liyi mutineers, Qiao Zhongfu against the Jingdong bandit Li Yu, and Shizhong against the Shanzhou bandit of Yutai.

sentences.zh: 世忠已破魚台，又擊黎驛叛兵，敗之，皆斬以獻。

translations.literal: Shizhong had already defeated Yutai, then also struck the Liyi rebels, defeated them, and beheaded them all to present.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the Yutai bandits, Shizhong also attacked the Liyi mutineers, defeated them, and presented all their severed heads.

sentences.zh: 於是群盜悉平，入備宿衛。

translations.literal: Thus the bandit hosts were all pacified, and he entered to serve in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: With the bandits pacified, he entered service in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 而河北賊丁順、楊進等皆赴招撫司，宗澤收而用之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Hebei bandits Ding Shun, Yang Jin, and others all went to the pacification office, and Zong Ze received and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Hebei bandits Ding Shun, Yang Jin, and others submitted to the pacification office, and Zong Ze took them into his service.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，升定國軍承宣使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he was promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianyan reign he was promoted to commissioner-in-chief of the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 帝如揚州，世忠以所部從。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Yangzhou; Shizhong followed with his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Yangzhou, Shizhong followed with his troops.

sentences.zh: 時張遇自金山來降，抵城下，不解甲，人心危懼，世忠獨入其壘，曉以逆順，眾悉聽命。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yu came from Jinshan to surrender, reached below the city, and did not remove his armor; hearts were fearful and alarmed; Shizhong alone entered his camp, enlightened them on obedience and rebellion, and the host all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yu came from Jinshan to surrender and reached the city still in armor, fear spread through the court. Shizhong alone entered his camp, explained the difference between loyalty and rebellion, and brought the whole force to submission.

sentences.zh: 李民眾十萬亦降，比至，有反覆狀。

translations.literal: Li Min's host of a hundred thousand also surrendered, but when they arrived there were signs of vacillation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min's force of a hundred thousand also surrendered, but on arrival they showed signs of wavering.

sentences.zh: 王淵遣世忠諭旨，世忠知其党劉彥異議，即先斬彥，驅李民出，縛小校二十九人，送淵斬之。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan sent Shizhong to proclaim the imperial intent; Shizhong knew his faction's Liu Yan held a different view, and immediately first beheaded Yan, drove Li Min out, bound twenty-nine junior officers, and sent them to Yuan to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan sent Shizhong to announce the imperial will. Shizhong learned that Liu Yan, a leader among Li Min's men, was stirring dissent; he beheaded Yan at once, drove Li Min's force out of camp, bound twenty-nine junior officers, and sent them to Wang Yuan for execution.

sentences.zh: 事定，授京西等路捉殺內外盜賊。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed to capture and kill internal and external bandits on the Jingxi and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was appointed to hunt down bandits within and beyond the capital region on the Jingxi and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 金人再攻河南，翟進合世忠兵夜襲悟室營，不克，反為所敗。

translations.literal: The Jin again attacked Henan; Zhai Jin combined with Shizhong's troops to night-assault the Wushi camp, did not overcome it, and in turn was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin again attacked Henan, Zhai Jin joined Shizhong in a night assault on the Wushi camp. The attack failed and they were routed in turn.

sentences.zh: 會丁進失期，陳思恭先遁，世忠被矢如棘，力戰得免。

translations.literal: Ding Jin missed the rendezvous, Chen Sigong fled first, Shizhong was struck by arrows like a hedge, fought fiercely, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Jin failed to arrive on time and Chen Sigong fled first. Shizhong was struck by arrows thick as a hedge but fought his way free.

sentences.zh: 還汴，詰一軍之先退者皆斬，左右懼。

translations.literal: Returning to Bian, he interrogated the whole army and beheaded all who had retreated first; those at his side were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Bianjing he had every soldier who had retreated first beheaded, and his officers trembled.

sentences.zh: 進由是與世忠有隙，尋以叛誅。

translations.literal: Jin thereby had a rift with Shizhong and soon was executed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: From this Ding Jin bore a grudge against Shizhong and was soon executed for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 召世忠還，授鄜延路副總管，加平寇左將軍，屯淮陽，會山東兵拒敵。

translations.literal: Shizhong was recalled, appointed deputy overall commander of the Zhenyan circuit, given the additional title Left General for Pacifying Bandits, stationed at Huaiyang, and joined Shandong troops in resisting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong was recalled, appointed deputy overall commander of the Zhenyan circuit and given the additional title Left General for Pacifying Bandits. He was stationed at Huaiyang to coordinate with Shandong forces against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 粘罕聞世忠扼淮陽，乃分兵萬人趨揚州，自以大軍迎世忠戰。

translations.literal: Nianhan heard Shizhong was blocking Huaiyang, then divided ten thousand troops to hurry toward Yangzhou, and himself with the great army went to meet Shizhong in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Nianhan learned that Shizhong was holding Huaiyang, he detached ten thousand men toward Yangzhou and led the main army to engage Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 世忠不敵，夜引歸，敵躡之，軍潰于沐陽，閤門宣贊舍人張遇死之。

translations.literal: Shizhong could not withstand them, withdrew by night, the enemy pursued, the army collapsed at Muyang, and the Gate Department proclaimer Zhang Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong could not hold and withdrew by night. The enemy pursued, his army broke at Muyang, and Zhang Yu, a proclaimer of the Gate Department, was killed.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝召諸將議移蹕，張俊、辛企宗請往湖南，世忠曰：「淮、浙富饒，今根本地，詎可舍而之他？

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor summoned the generals to discuss moving the imperial seat; Zhang Jun and Xin Qizong asked to go to Hunan; Shizhong said: "Huai and Zhe are rich and fertile—the foundation ground of today—how can we abandon them and go elsewhere?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor summoned his generals to discuss moving the court. Zhang Jun and Xin Qizong urged retreat to Hunan. Shizhong said, "The Huai and Zhe regions are rich and fertile—the heartland of the dynasty today. How can we abandon them and go elsewhere?"

sentences.zh: 人心懷疑，一有退避，則不逞者思亂，重湖、閩嶺之遙，安保道路無變乎？

translations.literal: If hearts harbor doubt, once there is any retreat, the unbridled will think of disorder; the distant lakes and Min ranges—how can we secure that the roads will be without change?"
translations.idiomatic: If the court shows doubt, the moment it retreats the unruly will think of rebellion. And who can guarantee that the roads through the deep lakes and distant Min ranges will stay safe?"

sentences.zh: 淮、江當留兵為守，車駕當分兵為衛，約十萬人，分半扈江、淮上下，止余五萬，可保防守無患乎？

translations.literal: Huai and the Yangtze should keep troops as garrison; the imperial carriage should divide troops as guard—about a hundred thousand men; half to escort up and down the Jiang and Huai, only fifty thousand left—can defense be kept without worry?"
translations.idiomatic: We would need troops to hold the Huai and Yangzi lines and an escort for the imperial procession—say a hundred thousand men. Half would guard the rivers, leaving only fifty thousand. Could we really defend anything with that?"

sentences.zh: 」在陽城收合散亡，得數千人，聞帝如錢塘，即繇海道赴行在。

translations.literal: At Yangcheng he gathered the scattered and lost and obtained several thousand men; hearing the emperor was going to Qiantang, he immediately by sea route hastened to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangcheng he gathered his scattered troops until he had several thousand men. Learning that the emperor was heading for Qiantang, he took the sea route to join the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 苗傅、劉正彥反，張浚等在平江議討亂，知世忠至，更相慶慰，張俊喜躍不自持。

translations.literal: Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled; Zhang Jun and others at Pingjiang discussed suppressing the disorder; learning Shizhong had arrived, they congratulated one another; Zhang Jun leaped for joy and could not contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, Zhang Jun and others at Pingjiang were planning the suppression. Learning that Shizhong had arrived, they congratulated one another, and Zhang Jun leaped for joy beyond control.

sentences.zh: 世忠得俊書，大慟，舉酒酹神曰：「誓不與此賊共戴天！

translations.literal: Shizhong received Jun's letter, wailed greatly, raised wine and poured a libation to the spirits, saying: "I swear not to live under the same sky with these rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong received Zhang Jun's letter he wept bitterly, poured a libation to heaven, and swore, "I will not live under the same sky as these traitors!"

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆奮。

translations.literal: The soldiers all were stirred.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers were roused to fury.

sentences.zh: 見浚曰：「今日大事，世忠願與張俊身任之，公無憂。

translations.literal: Seeing Jun he said: "Today's great affair—Shizhong is willing with Zhang Jun to bear it in person; sir, do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhang Jun, "On this great day Shizhong and Zhang Jun will bear the burden ourselves. Sir, have no fear."

sentences.zh: 」欲即進兵。

translations.literal: He wished to advance troops immediately.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to march at once.

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「投鼠忌器，事不可急，急則恐有不測，已遣馮轓甘言誘賊矣。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "One fears harming the vessel when throwing at the mouse—the affair cannot be hurried; if hurried there may be unforeseen events; I have already sent Feng Fan with sweet words to entice the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun said, "We must not strike too rashly for fear of harming the emperor. The matter cannot be rushed or something unforeseen may happen. I have already sent Feng Fan with soothing words to lure the rebels."

sentences.zh: 三月戊戌，以所部發平江。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the third month he set out from Pingjiang with his command.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the third month he marched from Pingjiang with his troops.

sentences.zh: 張俊慮世忠兵少，以劉寶兵二千借之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, concerned Shizhong's troops were few, lent him two thousand of Liu Bao's soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, worried that Shizhong had too few men, lent him two thousand troops under Liu Bao.

sentences.zh: 舟行載甲士，綿互三十里。

translations.literal: Boats carried armored soldiers stretching continuously for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: His boats carried armored troops in a line thirty li long.

sentences.zh: 至秀州，稱病不行，造雲梯，治器械，傅等始懼。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiu Prefecture, he claimed illness and would not advance, built cloud ladders, prepared weapons, and Fu and the others at last grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiu Prefecture he claimed illness and halted his advance while building siege ladders and preparing weapons. Miao Fu and his allies were at last alarmed.

sentences.zh: 初，傅、正彥聞世忠來，檄以其兵屯江陰。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fu and Zhengyan, hearing Shizhong was coming, issued a dispatch ordering his troops stationed at Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan first heard Shizhong was coming, they issued orders for his troops to be stationed at Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 世忠以好語報之，且言所部殘零，欲赴行在。

translations.literal: Shizhong replied with kind words and moreover said his command was broken and scattered and he wished to go to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong answered with reassuring words, saying his force was broken and scattered and that he wished only to join the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 傅等大喜，許之，至矯制除世忠及張俊為節度使，皆不受。

translations.literal: Fu and the others were greatly pleased and assented; they even forged edicts appointing Shizhong and Zhang Jun as military commissioners, but both refused.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and his allies were delighted and agreed. They even forged edicts appointing Shizhong and Zhang Jun as military commissioners, but both refused.

sentences.zh: 時世忠妻梁氏及子亮為傅所質，防守嚴密。

translations.literal: At that time Shizhong's wife, the Lady Liang, and his son Liang were held hostage by Fu, under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong's wife, Lady Liang, and his son Liang were held hostage by Miao Fu under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非紿傅曰：「今白太后，遣二人慰撫世忠，則平江諸人益安矣。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei deceived Fu, saying: "Now report to the empress dowager and send the two to comfort Shizhong, and then the people of Pingjiang will be even more at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei deceived Miao Fu, saying, "If we inform the empress dowager and send the two of them to reassure Shizhong, the men at Pingjiang will be even more at ease."

sentences.zh: 」於是召梁氏入，封安國夫人，俾迓世忠，速其勤王。

translations.literal: Thus the Lady Liang was summoned in, enfeoffed as Lady of the State for Pacifying the Realm, and made to go meet Shizhong and hasten his rescue of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang was summoned to court, enfeoffed as Lady of the State for Pacifying the Realm, and sent to join Shizhong and urge him to march to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 梁氏疾驅出城，一日夜會世忠於秀州。

translations.literal: The Lady Liang drove swiftly out of the city and in one day and night joined Shizhong at Xiu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang galloped out of the city and reached Shizhong at Xiu Prefecture within a day and a night.

sentences.zh: 未幾，明受詔至，世忠曰：「吾知有建炎，不知有明受。

translations.literal: Before long the Mingshou edict arrived; Shizhong said: "I know there is Jianyan; I do not know there is Mingshou."
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict arrived under the rebel reign title Mingshou. Shizhong said, "I know the Jianyan reign; I do not know any Mingshou."

sentences.zh: 」斬其使，取詔焚之，進兵益急。

translations.literal: He beheaded the envoy, took the edict and burned it, and advanced troops all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the envoy, burned the edict, and pressed his advance all the harder.

sentences.zh: 傅等大懼。

translations.literal: Fu and the others were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and his allies were terrified.

sentences.zh: 次臨平，賊將苗翊、馬柔吉負山阻河為陣，中流植鹿角，梗行舟。

translations.literal: Halting at Linping, the rebel generals Miao Yi and Ma Rouji held the mountain and blocked the river in formation; in midstream they planted antlers and obstructed the passage of boats.
translations.idiomatic: At Linping the rebel generals Miao Yi and Ma Rouji formed a line with the mountain at their back and the river before them, planting stakes in midstream to block his boats.

sentences.zh: 世忠舍舟力戰，張俊繼之，劉光世又繼之。

translations.literal: Shizhong abandoned the boats and fought with force; Zhang Jun followed him, and Liu Guangshi followed again.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong left his boats and fought on foot; Zhang Jun pressed the attack after him, and Liu Guangshi followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 軍少卻，世忠復舍馬操戈而前，令將士曰：「今日當以死報國，面不被數矢者皆斬。

translations.literal: The army fell back slightly; Shizhong again left his horse, took spear in hand and advanced, ordering the officers and soldiers: "Today we must repay the state with death; whoever's face is not struck by several arrows—all will be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: When the army gave ground slightly, Shizhong dismounted again, spear in hand, and told his men, "Today we repay the state with our lives. Anyone whose face is not struck by several arrows will be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」於是士皆用命。

translations.literal: Thus the soldiers all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers obeyed without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 賊列神臂弩持滿以待，世忠瞋目大呼，挺刃突前，賊辟易，矢不及發，遂敗。

translations.literal: The rebels arrayed divine-arm crossbows drawn full to wait; Shizhong glared and shouted greatly, levelled his blade and burst forward; the rebels gave way, arrows could not be loosed, and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lined up their divine-arm crossbows at full draw. Shizhong glared and roared, charged with blade levelled, and the rebels scattered before they could shoot. They were routed.

sentences.zh: 傅、正彥擁精兵二千，開湧金門以遁。

translations.literal: Fu and Zhengyan with two thousand elite troops opened the Yongjin Gate to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan took two thousand elite troops and fled through the Yongjin Gate.

sentences.zh: 世忠馳入，帝步至宮門，握世忠手慟哭曰：「中軍吳湛佐逆為最，尚留朕肘腋，能先誅乎？

translations.literal: Shizhong galloped in; the emperor walked to the palace gate, grasped Shizhong's hand and wept bitterly, saying: "Central Army Wu Zhan aided the rebels most of all and still remains at my very side—can you first execute him?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong galloped in. The emperor walked to the palace gate, seized his hand, and wept, "Wu Zhan of the Central Army was the rebels' chief accomplice and still remains at my side. Can you cut him down first?"

sentences.zh: 」世忠即謁湛，握手與語，折其中指，戮於市，又執賊謀主王世修以屬吏。

translations.literal: Shizhong immediately visited Zhan, took his hand and spoke with him, broke his middle finger, executed him in the market, and also seized the rebel chief plotter Wang Shixiu and handed him to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong went straight to Wu Zhan, took his hand as if in friendly talk, broke his middle finger, and had him executed in the market. He also seized the rebel mastermind Wang Shixiu and handed him over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 詔授武勝軍節度使禦營左軍都統制。

translations.literal: By edict he was appointed military commissioner of the Wusheng Army and overall commander of the Imperial Camp Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Wusheng Army and overall commander of the Imperial Camp Left Army.

sentences.zh: 請於帝曰：「賊擁精兵，距甌、閩甚邇，儻成巢窟，卒未可滅，臣請討之。

translations.literal: He requested of the emperor: "The rebels hold elite troops and are very near to Ou and Min; if they form a lair, in the end they cannot be destroyed—I request to suppress them."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor, "The rebels still hold elite troops and are very close to Ou and Min. If they establish a base there, they may never be destroyed. I beg leave to pursue them."

sentences.zh: 」於是以為江、浙制置使，自衢、信追擊，至漁梁驛，與賊遇。

translations.literal: Thus he was made commissioner for Jiang and Zhe, pursued from Qu and Xin, reached Yuliang Post, and met the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commissioner for Jiang and Zhe and pursued the rebels from Quzhou and Xinzhou. At Yuliang Post he caught up with them.

sentences.zh: 世忠步走挺戈而前，賊望見，咋曰：「此韓將軍也！

translations.literal: Shizhong walked forward with spear levelled; the rebels saw him and exclaimed: "This is General Han!"
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong advanced on foot spear in hand. When the rebels saw him they cried, "It is General Han!"

sentences.zh: 」皆驚潰。

translations.literal: All were startled and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: They broke and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 擒正彥及傅弟翊送行在，傅亡建陽，追禽之，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhengyan and Fu's younger brother Yi were captured and sent to the traveling court; Fu fled to Jianyang, was pursued and captured, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhengyan and Miao Fu's brother Yi were captured and sent to the traveling court. Miao Fu fled to Jianyang but was pursued, captured, and executed along with the others.

sentences.zh: 世忠初陛辭，奏曰：「臣誓生獲賊，為社稷刷恥，乞殿前二虎賁護俘來獻。

translations.literal: When Shizhong first took leave at court he memorialized: "Your servant vows to capture the rebels alive, wash away the state's shame, and begs two Tiger Guards of the Hall to escort the prisoners to present them."
translations.idiomatic: When he first took leave of the emperor he vowed, "I swear to capture the rebels alive and wipe away this shame upon the realm. I ask for two Tiger Guards of the Hall to escort the prisoners when I present them."

sentences.zh: 」至是，卒如其言。

translations.literal: At this time, in the end it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did exactly as he had promised.

sentences.zh: 帝手書「忠勇」二字，揭旗以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote the two characters "Loyal and Brave," displayed them on a banner, and bestowed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the characters "Loyal and Brave" in his own hand and bestowed them on a banner.

sentences.zh: 授檢校少保、武勝昭慶軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting Junior Guardian and military commissioner of the Wusheng and Zhaoqing armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Junior Guardian and military commissioner of the Wusheng and Zhaoqing armies.

sentences.zh: 兀朮將入侵，帝召諸將問移蹕之地，張俊、辛企宗勸自鄂、岳幸長沙，世忠曰：「國家已失河北，山東，若又棄江、淮，更有何地？

translations.literal: Wuzhu was about to invade; the emperor summoned the generals to ask where to move the imperial seat; Zhang Jun and Xin Qizong urged going from E and Yue to favor Changsha; Shizhong said: "The state has already lost Hebei and Shandong—if we again abandon Jiang and Huai, what land remains?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhu was about to invade, the emperor asked his generals where to move the court. Zhang Jun and Xin Qizong urged retreat from Ezhou and Yuezhou to Changsha. Shizhong said, "The dynasty has already lost Hebei and Shandong. If we abandon the Jiang and Huai regions as well, what land is left to us?"

sentences.zh: 」於是以世忠為浙西制置使，守鎮江。

translations.literal: Thus Shizhong was made commissioner for western Zhe and guarded Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong was appointed commissioner for western Zhe and stationed at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 既而兀朮分道渡江，諸屯皆敗，世忠亦自鎮江退保江陰。

translations.literal: Before long Wuzhu crossed the Yangtze by separate routes; all garrisons were defeated; Shizhong also withdrew from Zhenjiang to hold Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu soon crossed the Yangtze in several columns. Every garrison was defeated, and Shizhong withdrew from Zhenjiang to hold Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 杜充以建康降敵，兀朮自廣德破臨安，帝如浙東。

translations.literal: Du Chong surrendered Jiankang to the enemy; Wuzhu from Guangde broke Lin'an; the emperor went to eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong surrendered Jiankang to the enemy. Wuzhu broke through from Guangde to Lin'an, and the emperor fled to eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 世忠以前軍駐青龍鎮，中軍駐江灣，後軍駐海口，俟敵歸邀擊之。

translations.literal: Shizhong stationed the vanguard at Qinglong Town, the center army at Jiangwan, the rear army at Haikou, waiting for the enemy's return to intercept and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong posted his vanguard at Qinglong Town, his center force at Jiangwan, and his rear guard at Haikou, waiting to ambush the Jin on their return.

sentences.zh: 帝召至行在，奏：「方留江上截金人歸師，盡死一戰。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to the traveling court; he memorialized: "I am just now staying on the river to cut off the Jin return army and will fight to the death in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to court. He reported, "I mean to hold the river line and cut off the Jin retreat. I will fight to the death."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂輔臣曰：「此呂頤浩在會稽，嘗建此策，世忠不謀而同。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "This is what Lü Yihao at Kuaiji once proposed as a plan—Shizhong agrees without having consulted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Lü Yihao once proposed this same plan at Kuaiji. Shizhong has reached the same conclusion without consulting him."

sentences.zh: 」賜親劄，聽其留。

translations.literal: He bestowed a personal letter and permitted him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a personal letter and allowed him to stay.

sentences.zh: 會上元節，就秀州張燈高會，忽引兵趨鎮江。

translations.literal: It happened to be the Lantern Festival; at Xiu Prefecture he hung lanterns in a grand gathering, then suddenly led troops hurrying to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival he held a grand lantern feast at Xiu Prefecture, then suddenly marched his army to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 及金兵至，則世忠軍已先屯焦山寺。

translations.literal: When the Jin troops arrived, Shizhong's army had already encamped at Jiaoshan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Jin arrived, Shizhong's army was already encamped at Jiaoshan Temple.

sentences.zh: 金將李選降，受之。

translations.literal: The Jin general Li Xuan surrendered and was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Li Xuan surrendered and was accepted into service.

sentences.zh: 兀朮遣使通問，約日大戰，許之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu sent an envoy to communicate; they agreed on a day for great battle; he assented.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu sent envoys to negotiate and they agreed on a day for a major battle.

sentences.zh: 戰將十合，梁夫人親執桴鼓，金兵終不得渡。

translations.literal: The battle was about to reach ten engagements; the Lady Liang personally beat the war drum; the Jin troops in the end could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: After nearly ten engagements Lady Liang herself beat the war drums, and the Jin army could not force a crossing.

sentences.zh: 盡歸所掠假道，不聽；

translations.literal: They offered to return all plunder and pass through on loan of the road—he would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu offered to return all his plunder and pass through on loan of the road, but Shizhong refused.

sentences.zh: 請以名馬獻，又不聽。

translations.literal: they asked to present famous horses in tribute—again he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He offered famous horses as tribute, and Shizhong refused again.

sentences.zh: 撻辣在濰州，遣孛堇太一趨淮東以援兀朮，世忠與二酋相持黃天蕩者四十八日。

translations.literal: Tala was at Weizhou and sent the jinwei Taiyi toward Huaidong to aid Wuzhu; Shizhong and the two chiefs faced each other at Huangtiangang for forty-eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Tala at Weizhou sent the jinwei Taiyi to reinforce Wuzhu in Huaidong. Shizhong and the two Jin commanders faced each other at Huangtiangang for forty-eight days.

sentences.zh: 太一孛堇軍江北，兀朮軍江南，世忠以海艦進泊金山下，預以鐵綆貫大鉤授驍健者。

translations.literal: Taiyi's army was north of the river, Wuzhu's south of the river; Shizhong advanced sea warships to moor below Jinshan, beforehand giving iron cables threaded with great hooks to the brave and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi held the north bank and Wuzhu the south. Shizhong moved his sea warships to anchor below Jinshan and armed his strongest men with iron cables fitted with great hooks.

sentences.zh: 明旦，敵舟噪而前，世忠分海舟為兩道出其背，每縋一綆，則曳一舟沉之。

translations.literal: At dawn the enemy boats clamored forward; Shizhong divided the sea boats into two paths to come out behind them; each time one cable was lowered, one boat was dragged and sunk.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the enemy fleet advanced with a great clamor. Shizhong split his sea boats into two columns to strike from behind. Each time a cable was lowered, a Jin boat was dragged under and sunk.

sentences.zh: 兀朮窮蹙，求會語，祈請甚哀。

translations.literal: Wuzhu was cornered in distress, sought a meeting to speak, and pleaded very piteously.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered and desperate, Wuzhu asked for a parley and pleaded piteously.

sentences.zh: 世忠曰：「還我兩宮，復我疆土，則可以相全。

translations.literal: Shizhong said: "Return our two palaces, restore our territory—then we can mutually preserve one another."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong said, "Return our two emperors and restore our territory, and then we can let you go."

sentences.zh: 」兀朮語塞。

translations.literal: Wuzhu was speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu had no reply.

sentences.zh: 又數日求再會，言不遜，世忠引弓欲射之，亟弛去，謂諸將曰：「南軍使船欲如使馬，奈何？

translations.literal: Several days later he sought another meeting; his words were not deferential; Shizhong drew his bow intending to shoot him; he quickly fled away and told his generals: "The southern army uses boats as if using horses—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Days later Wuzhu sought another meeting and spoke insolently. Shizhong drew his bow to shoot him, and Wuzhu fled at once. He told his generals, "The southern army uses boats the way we use horses. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」募人獻破海舟策。

translations.literal: He recruited men to present plans for breaking the sea boats.
translations.idiomatic: He offered rewards for a plan to defeat the sea boats.

sentences.zh: 閩人王某者，教其舟中載土，平版鋪之，穴船版以棹槳，風息則出江，有風則勿出。

translations.literal: A man of Min surnamed Wang taught them to load earth in the boats, spread flat boards over it, bore holes in the boat boards for oars and paddles, when the wind ceased then go out on the river, when there was wind then do not go out.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Fujian surnamed Wang taught them to load their boats with earth, lay flat boards over it, and bore holes through the planking for oars and paddles. They were to put out only when the wind died and stay in port when it blew.

sentences.zh: 海舟無風，不可動也。

translations.literal: Sea boats without wind cannot move.
translations.idiomatic: The sea boats could not move without wind.

sentences.zh: 又有獻謀者曰：「鑿大渠接江口，則在世忠上流。

translations.literal: Another presented a plan saying: "Dig a great canal connecting to the river mouth, and it will be upstream of Shizhong."
translations.idiomatic: Another adviser said, "Dig a great canal to the river mouth and you will be upstream of Shizhong."

sentences.zh: 」兀朮一夕潛鑿渠三十里，且用方士計，刑白馬，剔婦人心，自割其額祭天。

translations.literal: Wuzhu in one night secretly dug a canal thirty li, and moreover used a geomancer's plan, punished a white horse, gouged out a woman's heart, and cut his own forehead to sacrifice to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In one night Wuzhu secretly dug a canal thirty li long. Following a geomancer's rite, he sacrificed a white horse, gouged out a woman's heart, and cut his own forehead to offer blood to heaven.

sentences.zh: 次日風止，我軍帆弱不能運，金人以小舟縱火，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The next day the wind ceased; our army's sails were weak and could not be worked; the Jin used small boats to set fire, arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the wind died. The Song sails were too weak to move, and the Jin sent small fire ships while arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 孫世詢、嚴允皆戰死，敵得絕江遁去。

translations.literal: Sun Shixun and Yan Yun both died in battle; the enemy were able to cross the river and flee away.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shixun and Yan Yun were both killed in battle, and the enemy broke across the river and escaped.

sentences.zh: 世忠收餘軍還鎮江。

translations.literal: Shizhong gathered the remaining army and returned to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong gathered his survivors and returned to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 初，世忠謂敵至必登金山廟，觀我虛實。

translations.literal: Earlier Shizhong said when the enemy arrived they would surely climb Jinshan Temple to observe our strength and weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shizhong had said that when the enemy came they would surely climb Jinshan Temple to spy on his dispositions.

sentences.zh: 乃遣兵百人伏廟中，百人伏岸滸，約聞鼓聲，岸兵先入，廟兵合擊之。

translations.literal: He then sent a hundred soldiers to lie in ambush in the temple, a hundred to lie in ambush on the shore, agreeing that on hearing the drum the shore soldiers would enter first and the temple soldiers would join to strike.
translations.idiomatic: He posted a hundred men in ambush in the temple and a hundred on the shore, with orders that at the sound of the drum the shore party would strike first and the temple party would join the attack.

sentences.zh: 金人果五騎闖入，廟兵喜，先鼓而出，僅得二人。

translations.literal: The Jin indeed had five riders burst in; the temple soldiers rejoiced, beat the drum first and went out, and obtained only two men.
translations.idiomatic: Five Jin horsemen did ride into the temple. The ambushers rejoiced, beat the drum too soon, and caught only two men.

sentences.zh: 逸其三，中有絳袍玉帶、既墜而復馳者，詰之，乃兀朮也。

translations.literal: Three escaped; among them was one in crimson robe and jade belt who had fallen yet spurred on again; interrogating him, it was Wuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Three escaped, including one in a crimson robe and jade belt who had fallen from his horse yet spurred on again. On inquiry it proved to be Wuzhu himself.

sentences.zh: 是役也，兀朮兵號十萬，世忠僅八千餘人。

translations.literal: In this campaign Wuzhu's troops were said to number a hundred thousand; Shizhong had only a little more than eight thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Wuzhu's army was said to number a hundred thousand men, while Shizhong had barely eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝凡六賜劄，褒獎甚寵。

translations.literal: The emperor altogether six times bestowed letters, praising and rewarding with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him six personal letters of praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 拜檢校少保、武成感德軍節度使，神武左軍都統制。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting Junior Guardian, military commissioner of the Wucheng and Gande armies, and overall commander of the Divine Martial Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Junior Guardian, military commissioner of the Wucheng and Gande armies, and overall commander of the Divine Martial Left Army.

sentences.zh: 建安範汝為反，辛企宗等討捕未克，賊勢愈熾。

translations.literal: Fan Ruwei of Jian'an rebelled; Xin Qizong and others in suppression did not overcome him; the rebel momentum grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ruwei rebelled at Jian'an. Xin Qizong and others failed to suppress him, and the rebellion grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 以世忠為福建、江西、荊湖宣撫副使，世忠曰：「建居閩嶺上流，賊沿流而下，七郡皆血肉矣。

translations.literal: Shizhong was made deputy commissioner for Fujian, Jiangxi, and Jinghu; Shizhong said: "Jian sits on the upper reaches of the Min ranges—if the rebels flow down along the stream, the seven prefectures will all become flesh and blood."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong was appointed deputy commissioner for Fujian, Jiangxi, and Jinghu. He said, "Jian'an lies on the upper Min watershed. If the rebels sweep downstream, seven prefectures will be slaughtered to the last man."

sentences.zh: 」亟領步卒三萬，水陸並進。

translations.literal: He immediately led thirty thousand foot soldiers, advancing by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately led thirty thousand foot soldiers by land and water together.

sentences.zh: 次劍潭，賊焚橋，世忠策馬先渡，師遂濟。

translations.literal: Halting at Jiantan, the rebels burned the bridge; Shizhong spurred his horse to cross first, and the army thereupon crossed.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiantan the rebels burned the bridge. Shizhong spurred his horse across first, and the army followed.

sentences.zh: 賊盡塞要路拒王師，世忠命諸軍偃旗僕鼓，徑抵鳳凰山，頫瞰城邑，設雲梯火樓，連日夜並攻，賊震怖叵測。

translations.literal: The rebels completely blocked key roads to resist the imperial army; Shizhong ordered the armies to lower flags and lay down drums, went straight to Phoenix Mountain, looked down on the city, set cloud ladders and fire towers, attacked day and night together, and the rebels were shaken in terror beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels blocked every key road against the imperial army. Shizhong ordered his troops to lower their flags and drums and march straight to Phoenix Mountain, overlooking the city. He set up siege ladders and fire towers and attacked day and night without pause until the rebels were shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 五日城破，汝為竄身自焚，斬其弟岳、吉以徇，禽其謀主謝向、施逵及裨將陸必強等五百餘人。

translations.literal: On the fifth day the city was broken; Ruwei hid himself and self-immolated; his younger brothers Yue and Ji were beheaded to display; plotters Xie Xiang, Shi Kui, and junior officers Lu Biqiang and more than five hundred others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day the city fell. Ruwei hid himself and burned to death. His brothers Yue and Ji were beheaded as a warning. More than five hundred men were captured, including the plotters Xie Xiang and Shi Kui and the officer Lu Biqiang.

sentences.zh: 世忠初欲盡誅建民，李綱自福州馳見世忠曰：「建民多無辜。

translations.literal: Shizhong at first wished to execute all the people of Jian; Li Gang hurried from Fuzhou to see Shizhong and said: "Many of the people of Jian are innocent."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong at first intended to slaughter all the people of Jian'an. Li Gang rode posthaste from Fuzhou and told him, "Most of the people of Jian'an are innocent."

sentences.zh: 」世忠令軍士馳城上毋下，聽民自相別，農給牛穀，商賈馳征禁，脅從者汰遣，獨取附賊者誅之。

translations.literal: Shizhong ordered soldiers to gallop along the wall telling none to come down, allowed the people to separate themselves, farmers were given oxen and grain, merchants were released from levies and prohibitions, those coerced were sifted out and sent away, and only those who adhered to the rebels were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong ordered his men to ride along the walls telling people not to come down, let the inhabitants sort themselves out, gave farmers oxen and grain, lifted trade restrictions on merchants, released those who had been coerced, and executed only those who had willingly joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 民感更生，家為立祠。

translations.literal: The people were moved and felt reborn; families established shrines for him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were grateful to be spared, and families erected shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝曰：「雖古名將何以加。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, the emperor said: "Even ancient famous generals—how could they surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the emperor said, "Even the famous generals of antiquity could not surpass this."

sentences.zh: 」賜黃金器皿。

translations.literal: He bestowed golden vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with golden vessels.

sentences.zh: 世忠因奏江西、湖南寇賊尚多，乞乘勝討平。

translations.literal: Shizhong thereupon memorialized that bandits in Jiangxi and Hunan were still many, and begged to ride the victory to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong memorialized that bandits still plagued Jiangxi and Hunan and asked to press his victory and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 廣西賊曹成擁餘眾在郴、邵。

translations.literal: The Guangxi bandit Cao Cheng held remaining masses at Chen and Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi bandit Cao Cheng still held a large force at Chen and Shao.

sentences.zh: 世忠既平閩寇，旋師永嘉，若將就休息者。

translations.literal: Shizhong having pacified the Min bandits, turned his army to Yongjia, as if about to rest.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Fujian, Shizhong marched his army to Yongjia as if preparing to rest.

sentences.zh: 忽由處、信徑至豫章，連營江濱數十里，群賊不虞其至，大驚。

translations.literal: Suddenly from Chu and Xin he went straight to Yuzhang, encamped along the riverbank for several tens of li, and the bandit hosts did not expect his arrival and were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he struck from Chuzhou and Xinzhou straight to Yuzhang and encamped along the river for miles. The bandits never expected him and were thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 世忠遣人招之，成以其眾降，得戰士八萬，遣詣行在。

translations.literal: Shizhong sent men to summon them; Cheng with his masses surrendered, obtaining eighty thousand fighting men, and sent them to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong sent envoys to summon Cao Cheng, who surrendered with his whole force. Shizhong took eighty thousand fighting men into service and sent them to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 遂移師長沙。

translations.literal: He thereupon moved his army to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 時劉忠有眾數萬，據白麵山，營柵相望。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zhong had a host of several tens of thousands, held White Flour Mountain, and stockades and palisades faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong commanded tens of thousands of men on White Flour Mountain, his camps and palisades stretching in a long line.

sentences.zh: 世忠始至，欲急擊，宣撫使孟庾不可，世忠曰：「兵家利害，策之審矣，非參政所知，請期半月效捷。

translations.literal: When Shizhong first arrived he wished to attack urgently; the commissioner Meng Yu forbade it; Shizhong said: "The advantages and harms of warfare have been weighed with care—this is not what the councillor knows; I request to set a term of half a month for effecting victory."
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Shizhong wanted to attack at once, but Commissioner Meng Yu forbade it. Shizhong said, "The calculus of war has been weighed with care. This is beyond the councillor's ken. Give me half a month and I will deliver victory."

sentences.zh: 」遂與賊對壘，弈棋張飲，堅壁不動，眾莫測。

translations.literal: He thereupon faced the rebels in camp, played chess and spread drinking, held the walls firm without moving, and none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: He faced the rebels across the lines, played chess and held banquets, and kept his walls without stirring, so that no one could guess his plan.

sentences.zh: 一夕，與蘇格聯騎穿賊營，候者呵問，世忠先得賊軍號，隨聲應之，周覽以出，喜曰：「此天錫也。

translations.literal: One night, with Su Ge he rode linked through the rebel camp; sentries shouted questions; Shizhong had first obtained the rebel army's watchword, answered according to the sound, toured all around and came out, rejoicing: "This is heaven's gift."
translations.idiomatic: One night he and Su Ge rode together through the rebel camp. When sentries challenged them, Shizhong had already learned the rebel watchword and answered correctly. They rode the circuit of the camp and came out safely. Shizhong rejoiced, "Heaven has given us this."

sentences.zh: 」夜伏精兵二千於白麵山，與諸將拔營而進，賊兵方迎戰，所遣兵已馳入中軍，奪望樓，植旗蓋，傳呼如雷，賊回顧驚潰，麾將士夾擊，大破之，斬忠首，湖南遂平。

translations.literal: At night he hid two thousand elite troops on White Flour Mountain, and with the generals pulled up camp and advanced; the rebel soldiers were just meeting battle when the dispatched troops had already galloped into the center army, seized the watch tower, planted flags and canopies, calls passed like thunder, the rebels looked back startled and fled in rout; he waved the officers and soldiers to attack from both sides, routed them greatly, cut off Zhong's head, and Hunan was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That night he hid two thousand elite troops on White Flour Mountain. He advanced with his generals while the rebels were still forming to meet him. His hidden force galloped into the rebel center, seized the watchtower, and raised flags and banners with shouts like thunder. The rebels looked back in panic and broke. He ordered a pincer attack, routed them completely, beheaded Liu Zhong, and Hunan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 授太尉，賜帶、笏，仍敕樞密以功頒示內外諸將。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal, bestowed belt and tablet, and still ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to display his merit to internal and external generals.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Marshal and given belt and court tablet. The Bureau of Military Affairs was ordered to proclaim his achievement to all generals within and beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 師還建康，置背嵬軍，皆勇鷙絕倫者。

translations.literal: The army returned to Jiankang; he established the Back-from-the-Heights Army, all fierce and brave beyond comparison.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Jiankang he formed the Back-from-the-Heights Army, drawn from the fiercest and bravest men under his command.

sentences.zh: 九月，為江南東、西路宣撫使，置司建康。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he became commissioner for eastern and western Jiangnan, with headquarters at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made commissioner for eastern and western Jiangnan, with headquarters at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，進開府儀同三司，充淮南東、西路宣撫使，置司泗州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year he was advanced to Grand Preceptor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, filled the post of commissioner for eastern and western Huainan, and established headquarters at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year he was promoted to Grand Preceptor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and appointed commissioner for eastern and western Huainan, with headquarters at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時聞李橫進師討偽齊，議遣大將，以世忠忠勇，故遣之。

translations.literal: At that time it was heard Li Heng was advancing troops to attack the false Qi; they debated sending a great general, and because Shizhong was loyal and brave, therefore sent him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Heng was reported to be advancing against the puppet Qi state, the court debated which great general to send. Because of Shizhong's loyalty and courage, he was chosen.

sentences.zh: 仍賜廣馬七綱，甲千副，銀二萬兩，帛二萬匹；

translations.literal: He was still bestowed seven strings of Guang horses, a thousand sets of armor, twenty thousand taels of silver, and twenty thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: He was also given seven strings of Guang horses, a thousand suits of armor, twenty thousand taels of silver, and twenty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又出錢百萬緡，米二十八萬斛，為半歲之用。

translations.literal: moreover issued a million strings of cash, two hundred eighty thousand hu of grain, for half a year's use.
translations.idiomatic: The court also allocated a million strings of cash and two hundred eighty thousand hu of grain, enough for half a year.

sentences.zh: 命戶部侍郎姚舜明詣泗州，總領錢糧；

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Yao Shunming to go to Sizhou and oversee overall money and grain;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Yao Shunming was sent to Sizhou to oversee funds and provisions.

sentences.zh: 倉部郎官孫逸如平江府、常秀饒州，督發軍食。

translations.literal: the Lang official of the Granary Department Sun Yi went to Pingjiang Prefecture, Chang, Xiu, and Raozhou to supervise dispatch of army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Lang official Sun Yi of the Granary Department went to Pingjiang and the prefectures of Chang, Xiu, and Rao to supervise the dispatch of army rations.

sentences.zh: 李橫兵敗還鎮，世忠不果渡淮。

translations.literal: Li Heng's army was defeated and returned to his post; Shizhong did not in the end cross the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng's army was defeated and withdrew to its base, so Shizhong never crossed the Huai.

sentences.zh: 四年，以建康、鎮江、淮東宣撫使駐鎮江。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, as commissioner for Jiankang, Zhenjiang, and Huaidong he was stationed at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was stationed at Zhenjiang as commissioner for Jiankang, Zhenjiang, and Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，金人與劉豫合兵，分道入侵。

translations.literal: That year the Jin and Liu Yu combined armies and invaded by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jin joined forces with Liu Yu and invaded in several columns.

sentences.zh: 帝手劄命世忠飭守備，圖進取，辭旨懇切。

translations.literal: The emperor by personal letter ordered Shizhong to tighten defenses and plan advance, the wording earnest and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote him a personal letter ordering him to strengthen his defenses and plan an offensive, in earnest and impassioned terms.

sentences.zh: 世忠受詔，感泣曰：「主憂如此，臣子何以生為！

translations.literal: Shizhong received the edict, was moved to tears and said: "The sovereign's worry is thus—how can a subject live!"
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the order, Shizhong wept and said, "When the sovereign is so troubled, what right has a subject to live in ease?"

sentences.zh: 」遂自鎮江濟師，俾統制解元守高郵，候金步卒；

translations.literal: He thereupon from Zhenjiang crossed his army, made the commander Jie Yuan hold Gaoyou and watch for Jin foot soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river from Zhenjiang, posted Commander Jie Yuan at Gaoyou to watch for Jin infantry,

sentences.zh: 親提騎兵駐大儀，當敵騎，伐木為柵，自斷歸路。

translations.literal: personally led cavalry to station at Dayi, faced the enemy cavalry, felled trees for palisades, and himself cut off the return road.
translations.idiomatic: and personally led his cavalry to Dayi to face the enemy horse. He felled trees for palisades and cut off his own retreat.

sentences.zh: 會遣魏良臣使金，世忠撤炊爨，紿良臣有詔移屯守江，良臣疾馳去。

translations.literal: It happened Wei Liangchen was sent as envoy to the Jin; Shizhong removed cooking fires, deceived Liangchen that there was an edict to move camp and guard the river, and Liangchen galloped away in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liangchen was then sent as envoy to the Jin. Shizhong struck his cooking fires and deceived Liangchen into believing there was an edict to move camp and guard the river. Liangchen galloped away at once.

sentences.zh: 世忠度良臣已出境，即上馬令軍中曰：「眡吾鞭所向。

translations.literal: Shizhong judged Liangchen had already left the border, immediately mounted his horse and told the army: "All look where my whip points."
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong judged that Liangchen had crossed the border, he mounted at once and told his army, "Watch where my whip points."

sentences.zh: 」於是引軍次大儀，勒五陣，設伏二十餘所，約聞鼓即起擊。

translations.literal: Thus he led the army to halt at Dayi, arrayed five formations, set ambushes at more than twenty places, agreeing that on hearing the drum they would rise and strike.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army to Dayi, drew up five battle lines, and set more than twenty ambushes with orders to strike at the sound of the drum.

sentences.zh: 良臣至金軍中，金人問王師動息，具以所見對。

translations.literal: Liangchen reached the Jin army; the Jin asked about the movements of the imperial army, and he fully reported what he had seen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangchen reached the Jin camp they asked about Song troop movements, and he reported exactly what he had seen.

sentences.zh: 聶兒孛堇聞世忠退，喜甚，引兵至江口，距大儀五里；

translations.literal: The jinwei Nier heard Shizhong had withdrawn, was greatly pleased, led troops to the river mouth, five li from Dayi;
translations.idiomatic: The jinwei Nier, hearing that Shizhong had withdrawn, was delighted and led his troops to the river mouth, five li from Dayi.

sentences.zh: 別將撻孛也擁鐵騎過五陣東。

translations.literal: the separate commander Taboye with iron cavalry passed east of the five formations.
translations.idiomatic: A separate commander, Taboye, led iron cavalry past the east flank of the five formations.

sentences.zh: 世忠傳小麾鳴鼓，伏兵四起，旗色與金人旗雜出，金軍亂，我軍迭進。

translations.literal: Shizhong passed the small banner and beat the drum; ambush soldiers rose on four sides, banner colors mixed with Jin banners coming out, the Jin army was in disorder, our army advanced in relays.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong waved his small banner and beat the drum. Ambushes rose on every side, Song and Jin banners mingled, the Jin army fell into chaos, and the Song forces pressed forward in waves.

sentences.zh: 背嵬軍各持長斧，上揕人胸，下斫馬足。

translations.literal: The Back-from-the-Heights Army each held long axes, upward piercing men's chests, downward chopping horses' legs.
translations.idiomatic: The Back-from-the-Heights men each wielded long axes, striking upward at men's chests and downward at horses' legs.

sentences.zh: 敵被甲陷泥淖，世忠麾勁騎四面蹂躪，人馬俱斃，遂擒撻孛也等二百餘人。

translations.literal: The enemy, armored, sank into mud and mire; Shizhong commanded elite cavalry to trample them from four sides; men and horses all perished; then he captured Taboye and more than two hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, trapped in armor in mud and mire, were trampled by elite cavalry that Shizhong sent against them from every side. Men and horses alike perished, and more than two hundred captives were taken, including Taboye.

sentences.zh: 所遣董旼亦擊金人於天長縣之鵶口，擒女真四十餘人。

translations.literal: Dong Min, whom he had dispatched, also struck the Jin at Yakou in Tianchang County and captured more than forty Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Min, whom Shizhong had sent out, also attacked the Jin at Yakou in Tianchang County and took more than forty Jurchen prisoners.

sentences.zh: 解元至高郵，遇敵，設水軍夾河陣，日合戰十三，相拒未決。

translations.literal: Jie Yuan reached Gaoyou, encountered the enemy, set naval forces in a battle line flanking the river, fought thirteen engagements in one day, and the standoff remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie Yuan reached Gaoyou and met the enemy, he deployed his river flotilla in battle lines along both banks. They fought thirteen times in a single day without either side gaining the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 世忠遣成閔將騎士往援，復大戰，俘生女真及千戶等。

translations.literal: Shizhong sent Cheng Min leading cavalry to reinforce; they fought again on a great scale and captured living Jurchens, qianhu officers, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong sent Cheng Min at the head of cavalry to reinforce him. After another major battle they took live Jurchen captives, qianhu officers, and others.

sentences.zh: 世忠復親追至淮，金人驚潰，相蹈藉，溺死甚眾。

translations.literal: Shizhong again personally pursued to the Huai; the Jin were alarmed and routed, trampling one another; very many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong personally pursued them all the way to the Huai River. The Jin broke in panic, trampled one another in flight, and very many drowned.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，群臣入賀，帝曰：「世忠忠勇，朕知其必能成功。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived, the officials entered to congratulate; the Emperor said: "Shizhong is loyal and brave; I knew he would certainly succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory arrived, the court officials came to offer congratulations. The Emperor said, "Shizhong is loyal and brave—I knew he would succeed."

sentences.zh: 」沈與求曰：「自建炎以來，將士未嘗與金人迎敵一戰，今世忠連捷以挫其鋒，厥功不細。

translations.literal: Shen Yuqiu said: "Since the Jianyan reign, officers and soldiers have never once fought the Jin in open battle; now Shizhong with successive victories has blunted their edge—this achievement is not small."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuqiu said, "Since the Jianyan era our troops have never once met the Jin in pitched battle. Shizhong's successive victories have blunted their momentum—a no small achievement."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「第憂賞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I only worry about rewarding him."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "My only concern is how to reward him adequately."

sentences.zh: 」於是部將董旼、陳桷、解元、呼延通等皆峻擢有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon the subordinate commanders Dong Min, Chen Que, Jie Yuan, Huyan Tong, and others were all sharply promoted with differences in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Min, Chen Que, Jie Yuan, Huyan Tong, and the other subordinate commanders were all promoted sharply, each according to his merit.

sentences.zh: 論者以此舉為中興武功第一。

translations.literal: Commentators regarded this campaign as the foremost military achievement of the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators regarded this campaign as the greatest military feat of the dynasty's restoration.

sentences.zh: 時撻辣屯泗州，兀朮屯竹塾鎮，為世忠所扼，以書幣約戰，世忠許之，且使兩伶人以橘、茗報聘。

translations.literal: At that time Tala was encamped at Sizhou and Wuzhu at Zhushu Town, choked off by Shizhong; with letters and gifts they arranged a battle; Shizhong agreed and moreover sent two entertainers with oranges and tea in return courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tala was encamped at Sizhou and Wuzhu at Zhushu Town, both blocked by Shizhong. They sent letters and gifts proposing a battle, and Shizhong agreed, dispatching two entertainers in return with oranges and tea.

sentences.zh: 會雨雪，金饋道不通，野無所掠，殺馬而食，蕃漢軍皆怨。

translations.literal: It happened to rain and snow; Jin supply routes were impassable, in the wild there was nothing to plunder; they killed horses to eat; Jurchen and Han armies alike were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Then came rain and snow. Jin supply lines were cut off, there was nothing to forage in the countryside, and they killed their horses for food. Jurchen and Han troops alike grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 兀朮夜引軍還，劉麟、劉猊棄輜重遁。

translations.literal: Wuzhu by night led the army back; Liu Lin and Liu Ni abandoned baggage trains and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu withdrew his army by night. Liu Lin and Liu Ni abandoned their supply trains and fled.

sentences.zh: 五年，進少保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was promoted to Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 六年，授武甯安化軍節度使、京東淮東路宣撫處置使，置司楚州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Wuning and Anhua and Pacification and Disposition Commissioner of the Jingdong and Huaidong Circuits, with his headquarters established at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Military Commissioner of Wuning and Anhua and Pacification Commissioner for Jingdong and Huaidong, with his headquarters at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世忠披草萊，立軍府，與士同力役。

translations.literal: Shizhong cleared through grass and weeds, established a military headquarters, and shared labor with the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong cleared the wilderness, established a military headquarters, and labored alongside his men.

sentences.zh: 夫人梁親織薄為屋。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Liang personally wove thin cloth for a dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liang wove cloth herself to roof their shelter.

sentences.zh: 將士有怯戰者，世忠遺以巾幗，設樂大宴，俾婦人妝以恥之，故人人奮厲。

translations.literal: Among officers and soldiers there were cowards; Shizhong gave them women's headdresses, set music for a great feast, and had women made up to shame them; therefore every man strove fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers showed cowardice in battle, Shizhong sent them women's headdresses and held a feast with music, having them dressed as women to shame them. Thereafter every man fought with fierce resolve.

sentences.zh: 撫集流散，通商惠工，山陽遂為重鎮。

translations.literal: He comforted and gathered the scattered refugees, opened trade and benefited crafts; Shanyang thus became a strategic strongpoint.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled refugees, encouraged trade and industry, and turned Shanyang into a major stronghold.

sentences.zh: 劉豫兵數入寇，輒為世忠所敗。
