translations.literal: Liu Yu's troops repeatedly invaded and were always defeated by Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's forces raided repeatedly and were repulsed by Shizhong each time.

sentences.zh: 時張浚以右相視師，命世忠自承、楚圖淮陽。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun as right chancellor supervised the army and ordered Shizhong from Chen and Chu to plan for Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jun, serving as Right Chancellor while supervising the army, ordered Shizhong to advance from Chen and Chu against Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 劉豫方聚兵淮陽，世忠即引軍渡淮，旁符離而北，至其城下。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was just gathering troops at Huaiyang; Shizhong immediately led the army across the Huai, passed by Fuli to the north, and reached beneath its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was massing troops at Huaiyang when Shizhong crossed the Huai, swung north past Fuli, and arrived beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 為賊所圍，奮戈一躍，潰圍而出，不遺一鏃。

translations.literal: Surrounded by bandits, he brandished his halberd and leaped in one bound, burst through the encirclement and came out, not losing a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded by the enemy, he brandished his halberd, leaped forward, broke through the encirclement, and emerged without losing a single man.

sentences.zh: 呼延通與金將牙合孛堇搏戰，扼其吭而禽之，乘銳掩擊，金人敗去。

translations.literal: Huyan Tong grappled in battle with the Jin general Yagahabojin, seized his throat and captured him; riding the momentum they struck in cover pursuit; the Jin were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Tong fought hand to hand with the Jin general Yagahabojin, seized him by the throat, and took him captive. Pressing the advantage in pursuit, they drove the Jin off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 既而圍淮陽，賊堅守不下，約曰：「受圍一日，則舉一烽。

translations.literal: Subsequently they besieged Huaiyang; the bandits held firm and could not be taken; they agreed: "For each day under siege, one beacon shall be raised."
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Huaiyang, but the enemy held firm and the city would not fall. They agreed that for each day the siege continued, one signal fire would be lit.

sentences.zh: 」至是，六烽具舉，兀朮與劉猊皆至。

translations.literal: At this point, all six beacons were raised; Wuzhu and Liu Ni both arrived.
translations.idiomatic: By then six signal fires had been lit. Wuzhu and Liu Ni both arrived.

sentences.zh: 世忠求援于張俊，俊以世忠有見吞意，不從。

translations.literal: Shizhong sought aid from Zhang Jun; Jun thought Shizhong had an intention to swallow him up and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong asked Zhang Jun for reinforcements, but Jun, suspecting that Shizhong meant to absorb his forces, refused.

sentences.zh: 世忠勒陣向敵，遣人語之曰：「錦衣驄馬立陣前者，韓相公也。

translations.literal: Shizhong drew up his battle line facing the enemy, sent a man to tell them: "The man in brocade robes on a piebald horse standing before the battle line is Minister Han."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong formed his battle line facing the enemy and sent word: "The man in brocade robes on a piebald horse at the front of the formation is Minister Han."

sentences.zh: 」或危之，世忠曰：「不如是，不足以致敵。

translations.literal: Some warned him of the danger; Shizhong said: "If it were not so, it would not suffice to lure the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: When some warned him of the danger, Shizhong said, "Otherwise I could not draw the enemy out."

sentences.zh: 」敵果至，殺其導戰二人，遂引去。

translations.literal: The enemy indeed came, killed two of their battle guides, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did approach, but Shizhong killed two of their advance scouts and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋詔班師，復歸楚州，淮陽之民，從而歸者以萬計。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered withdrawal; he returned again to Chuzhou; people of Huaiyang who followed and returned numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon orders came to withdraw. He returned to Chuzhou, and tens of thousands of people from Huaiyang followed him home.

sentences.zh: 三月，除京東、淮東宣撫處置使兼節制鎮江府，仍楚州置司。

translations.literal: In the third month, he was appointed Pacification and Disposition Commissioner of Jingdong and Huaidong, concurrently commanding Zhenjiang Prefecture, still with headquarters at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Jingdong and Huaidong, with concurrent authority over Zhenjiang Prefecture, while keeping his headquarters at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，賜號「揚武翊運功臣」，加橫海、武甯、安化三鎮節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he was granted the title "Meritorious Subject Who Uplifts Military Power and Supports the Dynasty," and added as Military Commissioner of the three circuits of Henghai, Wuning, and Anhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he received the honorific title "Meritorious Subject Who Uplifts Military Power and Supports the Dynasty" and was made Military Commissioner of Henghai, Wuning, and Anhua combined.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝在平江，世忠自楚州來朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Emperor was at Pingjiang; Shizhong came from Chuzhou to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, while the Emperor was at Pingjiang, Shizhong traveled from Chuzhou to attend him.

sentences.zh: 十月，邊報急，劉光世欲棄廬州還太平，張俊亦請益兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, frontier reports were urgent; Liu Guangshi wished to abandon Luzhou and return to Taiping; Zhang Jun also requested more troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month urgent reports arrived from the frontier. Liu Guangshi wanted to abandon Luzhou and fall back to Taiping, and Zhang Jun also requested reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 都督張浚曰：「今日之事，有進擊，無退保。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jun said: "In today's affair, there is advancing to attack, there is no falling back to defend."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jun said, "Today's situation calls for advance, not retreat."

sentences.zh: 」於是世忠引兵渡淮，與金將訛里也力戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shizhong led troops across the Huai and fought fiercely with the Jin general Wolila.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong then crossed the Huai and fought a hard battle with the Jin general Wolila.

sentences.zh: 劉猊將寇淮東，為世忠兵扼，不得進。

translations.literal: Liu Ni was about to raid Huaidong and was choked off by Shizhong's troops, unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni prepared to invade Huaidong but was blocked by Shizhong's forces and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 七年，築高郵城，民益安之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Gaoyou city was built; the people were increasingly settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the walls of Gaoyou were built, and the people grew ever more secure.

sentences.zh: 初，世忠移屯山陽，遣間結山東豪傑，約以緩急為應，宿州馬秦及太行群盜，多願奉約束者。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shizhong moved his camp to Shanyang, he sent agents to bond with Shandong heroes of the realm, agreeing to respond in urgency; Ma Qin of Suzhou and the bandits of the Taihang Mountains—many were willing to accept his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong first moved his camp to Shanyang, he sent agents to liaise with militant leaders in Shandong, pledging mutual support in times of crisis. Ma Qin of Suzhou and the brigands of the Taihang range were among the many who agreed to follow his lead.

sentences.zh: 金人廢劉豫，中原震動，世忠謂機不可失，請全師北討，招納歸附，為恢復計。

translations.literal: The Jin deposed Liu Yu; the Central Plain was shaken; Shizhong said the opportunity must not be lost, requested the full army for northern expedition, receiving and accepting those who submitted, planning for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin deposed Liu Yu and shock rippled through the Central Plain, Shizhong argued that the moment must not be missed. He petitioned to lead the full army north, win over defectors, and press the recovery of lost territory.

sentences.zh: 會秦檜主和議，命世忠徙屯鎮江。

translations.literal: It happened that Qin Hui advocated peace talks and ordered Shizhong to move camp to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: But Qin Hui was pushing for peace, and ordered Shizhong to relocate his camp to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 世忠言：「金人詭詐，恐以計緩我師，乞留此軍蔽遮江、淮。

translations.literal: Shizhong said: "The Jin are deceitful and treacherous; I fear they will use a stratagem to delay our army; I beg to leave this army to screen and shield the Yangtze and Huai."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong warned, "The Jin are treacherous. They may use this peace ploy merely to stall our army. I beg that this force be kept to guard the Yangtze and Huai frontiers."

sentences.zh: 」又力陳和議之非，願效死節，率先迎敵；

translations.literal: He also strenuously set forth the wrong of peace talks, willing to offer his life in loyal death, taking the lead to meet the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: He argued forcefully against the peace settlement, declaring his willingness to die in battle and lead the charge against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 若不勝，從之未晚。

translations.literal: If we do not win, to follow them will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, it will still not be too late to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 又言王倫、藍公佐交河南地界，乞令明具無反覆文狀為後證。

translations.literal: He also said Wang Lun and Lan Gongzuo were exchanging Henan territorial boundaries and begged that they be made to produce clear written guarantees without reversal as later evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that when Wang Lun and Lan Gongzuo negotiated the Henan border, they be required to produce explicit written pledges against any reversal.

sentences.zh: 章十數上，皆慷慨激切，且請單騎詣闕面奏，帝率優詔褒答。

translations.literal: Memorials were submitted more than ten times, all impassioned and urgent, and moreover he requested to go alone on horseback to the palace to memorialize in person; the Emperor repeatedly sent gracious edicts in praise and reply.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten passionate memorials, even asking to ride alone to court to speak in person. The Emperor responded each time with gracious edicts of praise.

sentences.zh: 後金果渝盟，咸如其言。

translations.literal: Later the Jin indeed violated the alliance; all was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin later broke the treaty, events unfolded exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 金使蕭哲之來，以詔諭為名，世忠聞之，凡四上疏言：「不可許，願舉兵決戰，兵勢最重處，臣請當之。

translations.literal: The Jin envoy Xiao Zhe came, in the name of an imperial proclamation; when Shizhong heard of it, in all he submitted four memorials saying: "This cannot be permitted; I wish to raise troops for decisive battle; wherever the military situation is most critical, your subject requests to hold that post."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy Xiao Zhe arrived bearing what was styled an imperial proclamation, Shizhong submitted four memorials declaring that the arrangement must be refused. He offered to lead the army into decisive battle and take personal responsibility for the most perilous sector of the front.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「金人欲以劉豫相待，舉國士大夫盡為陪臣，恐人心離散，士氣凋沮。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Jin wish to treat us as they treated Liu Yu; the whole nation's scholars and officials would all become attendant vassals; I fear hearts would scatter and morale would wither."
translations.idiomatic: He warned that the Jin intended to treat the Song as they had Liu Yu, reducing every scholar and official in the realm to vassal status—a prospect that would break morale and scatter loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」且請馳驛面奏，不許。

translations.literal: He also requested to gallop by post relay to memorialize in person; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked permission to ride post-haste to court to speak in person, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 既而伏兵洪澤鎮，將殺金使，不克。

translations.literal: Subsequently he set an ambush at Hongze Town, intending to kill the Jin envoy; it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid an ambush at Hongze Town intending to kill the Jin envoy, but the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 九年，授少師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was appointed Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 十年，金人敗盟，兀朮率撒離曷、李成等破三京，分道深入。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Jin violated the alliance; Wuzhu led Salihu, Li Cheng, and others to break the Three Capitals and advance deeply by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jin broke the treaty. Wuzhu led Salihu, Li Cheng, and others to seize the Three Capitals and push deep inland along several routes.

sentences.zh: 八月，世忠圍淮陽，金人來救，世忠迎擊於泇口鎮，敗之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shizhong besieged Huaiyang; the Jin came to rescue; Shizhong met and struck them at Jiakou Town and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shizhong besieged Huaiyang. When Jin relief forces arrived, he intercepted them at Jiakou Town and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 又遣解元擊金人於潭城，劉寶擊於千秋湖，皆捷。

translations.literal: He also sent Jie Yuan to strike the Jin at Tancheng and Liu Bao to strike at Qianqiu Lake; all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched Jie Yuan to attack the Jin at Tancheng and Liu Bao at Qianqiu Lake—both operations succeeded.

sentences.zh: 親隨將成閔從統制許世安奪淮陽門而入，大戰門內。

translations.literal: He personally followed with General Cheng Min following Controller Xu Shi'an in seizing the Huaiyang gate and entering; a great battle was fought inside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He went forward in person with Cheng Min, who followed Controller Xu Shi'an in storming the Huaiyang gate. A fierce battle raged inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 世安中四矢，閔被三十餘創，復奪門出。

translations.literal: Shi'an was hit by four arrows; Min received more than thirty wounds; they again seized the gate and came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shi'an took four arrows; Cheng Min suffered more than thirty wounds. They fought their way back out through the gate.

sentences.zh: 世忠奏其功，擢武德大夫，閔由是知名。

translations.literal: Shizhong memorialized their merit; Xu Shi'an was promoted to Wude Dafu; Min thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong reported their exploits. Xu Shi'an was promoted to Wude Dafu, and Cheng Min won renown thereby.

sentences.zh: 世忠進太保，封英國公，兼河南、北諸路招討使。

translations.literal: Shizhong was promoted to Grand Guardian, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Henan and northern circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong was promoted to Grand Guardian, enfeoffed as Duke of Ying, and made Pacification Commissioner for Henan and the northern circuits.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兀朮恥順昌之敗，復謀再入，詔大合兵於淮西以待。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Wuzhu, shamed by the defeat at Shunchang, again plotted to invade; an edict ordered a great gathering of troops at Huixi to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Wuzhu, stung by his defeat at Shunchang, planned another invasion. An edict ordered a mass mobilization on the Huai River west to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既而金敗於柘皋，復圍濠州。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Jin were defeated at Zhegao and again besieged Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were then defeated at Zhegao, but renewed their siege of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 世忠受詔救濠，以舟師至招信縣，夜以騎兵擊金人于聞賢驛，敗之。

translations.literal: Shizhong received an edict to rescue Haozhou; with river forces he reached Zhaoxin County; by night with cavalry he struck the Jin at Wenxian Post Station and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to relieve Haozhou, Shizhong sailed his river fleet to Zhaoxin County and by night routed Jin cavalry at Wenxian Post.

sentences.zh: 金人攻濠州，五日而破。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Haozhou; in five days they broke it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Haozhou after a five-day assault.

sentences.zh: 破三日，世忠至，楊沂中軍已南奔。

translations.literal: Three days after it fell, Shizhong arrived; Yang Yizhong's army had already fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the city fell Shizhong arrived, by which time Yang Yizhong's army had already broken south in flight.

sentences.zh: 世忠與金人戰於淮岸，夜遣劉寶溯流將劫之，金人伐木塞赤龍洲，扼其歸路，世忠知之，全師而還。

translations.literal: Shizhong fought the Jin on the Huai bank; by night he sent Liu Bao upstream intending to raid them; the Jin cut trees to block Chilongzhou, choking his return route; Shizhong knew this and withdrew the full army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong fought the Jin on the Huai shore. By night he sent Liu Bao upstream on a raiding mission, but the Jin felled trees to block Chilongzhou and cut off his retreat. Shizhong saw the trap and withdrew his entire force intact.

sentences.zh: 金人自渦口渡淮北去，自是不得入侵。

translations.literal: The Jin from Wokou crossed north of the Huai and departed; from this time they could not invade.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin crossed north at Wokou and withdrew. From then on they dared not invade again.

sentences.zh: 世忠在楚州十餘年，兵僅三萬，而金人不敢犯。

translations.literal: Shizhong was at Chuzhou more than ten years; troops numbered only thirty thousand, yet the Jin did not dare to violate.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong held Chuzhou for more than ten years with barely thirty thousand men, yet the Jin never dared attack.

sentences.zh: 秦檜收三大將權，四月，拜樞密使，遂以所積軍儲錢百萬貫，米九十萬石，酒庫十五歸於國。

translations.literal: Qin Hui gathered the authority of the three great generals; in the fourth month, Shizhong was appointed Privy Councilor; thereupon he turned over accumulated military stores of one million strings of cash, nine hundred thousand shi of grain, and fifteen wine warehouses to the state.
translations.idiomatic: As Qin Hui stripped the three great generals of their power, Shizhong was appointed Privy Councilor in the fourth month. He then surrendered his accumulated stores to the state: one million strings of cash, nine hundred thousand shi of grain, and fifteen wine warehouses.

sentences.zh: 世忠既不以和議為然，為檜所抑。

translations.literal: Shizhong did not approve of the peace talks and was suppressed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong had never accepted the peace settlement and was now restrained by Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 及魏良臣使金，世忠又力言：「自此人情消弱，國勢委靡，誰復振之？

translations.literal: When Wei Liangchen was envoy to Jin, Shizhong again spoke forcefully: "From this time popular sentiment will weaken, national vigor will sink—who will rally it again?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Liangchen was sent as envoy to the Jin, Shizhong protested again: "From this point morale will fade and the state's vigor will falter. Who will revive it?"

sentences.zh: 北使之來，乞與面議。

translations.literal: When the northern envoy comes, I beg to discuss face to face.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern envoys arrive, I beg leave to meet and debate them in person.

sentences.zh: 」不許，遂抗疏言檜誤國。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; he then submitted a bold memorial saying Qin was harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: His request was denied. He submitted a defiant memorial accusing Qin Hui of ruining the country.

sentences.zh: 檜諷言者論之，帝格其奏不下。

translations.literal: Qin prompted memorialists to criticize him; the Emperor withheld his memorial and did not release it.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui prompted censors to attack him, and the Emperor blocked his memorial from circulation.

sentences.zh: 世忠連疏乞解樞密柄，繼上表乞骸。

translations.literal: Shizhong repeatedly memorialized begging to relinquish the Privy Council post, then submitted a memorial begging to retire on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong repeatedly asked to resign his Privy Council post and then petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 十月，罷為醴泉觀使、奉朝請，進封福國公，節鉞如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he was dismissed and made Director of the Liquan Taoist Abbey and Attendant at Court; advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Fu, military insignia as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was relieved and made Director of the Liquan Abbey, with attendance at court. He was advanced to Duke of Fu while retaining his military commissions.

sentences.zh: 自此杜門謝客，絕口不言兵，時跨驢攜酒，從一二奚童，縱遊西湖以自樂，平時將佐罕得見其面。

translations.literal: From this time he closed his doors to guests, never spoke of military affairs; sometimes crossing on a donkey carrying wine, with one or two servant boys, he wandered freely on West Lake for his own pleasure; in ordinary times his officers and aides rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he shut his doors to visitors and never spoke of war again. He would ride a donkey with wine and one or two boy servants, roaming West Lake for pleasure. Even his former commanders rarely saw him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改潭國公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, his title was changed to Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was retitled Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 顯仁皇后自金還，世忠詣臨平朝謁。

translations.literal: When Empress Xianren returned from Jin captivity, Shizhong went to Linping to attend and pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xianren returned from captivity among the Jin, Shizhong went to Linping to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 後在北方聞其名，慰問者良久。

translations.literal: Later, having heard his name in the north, she consoled and inquired after him at length.
translations.idiomatic: Having long heard of him in the north, she spoke with him at length and offered warm condolences.

sentences.zh: 十三年，封咸安郡王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改鎮南、武安、甯國節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhennan, Wu'an, and Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was reassigned as Military Commissioner of Zhennan, Wu'an, and Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 二十一年八月薨，進拜太師，追封通義郡王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, eighth month, he died; posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Tongyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the twenty-first year. He was posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tongyi.

sentences.zh: 孝宗朝，追封蘄王，諡忠武，配饗高宗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Xiaozong reign, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, posthumous name Zhongwu, granted associated sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozong he was posthumously elevated to Prince of Qi, given the posthumous name Zhongwu ("Loyal and Martial"), and granted a place in sacrifices at Emperor Gaozong's temple.

sentences.zh: 世忠初得疾，敕尚醫視療，將吏臥內問疾，世忠曰：「吾以布衣百戰，致位王公，賴天之靈，保首領沒于家，諸君尚哀其死邪？

translations.literal: When Shizhong first fell ill, an edict ordered the imperial physicians to treat him; officers came to his bedside to inquire after his illness; Shizhong said: "I from common cloth fought a hundred battles and reached the rank of prince and duke; relying on Heaven's spirit, I keep my head and die at home—do you gentlemen still mourn my death?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong first fell ill, the Emperor sent court physicians to treat him. Officers came to his bedside, and Shizhong said, "I rose from common birth through a hundred battles to princely rank. By Heaven's grace I will keep my head and die at home—why mourn my death?"

sentences.zh: 」及死，剛朝服、貂蟬冠、水銀、龍腦以斂。

translations.literal: At death, he was enshrouded in stiff court robes, marten-fur official cap, mercury, and borneol camphor.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was laid out in full court regalia—official robes, the tiered cap of rank, mercury, and borneol camphor for preservation.

sentences.zh: 世忠嘗戒家人曰：「吾名世忠，汝曹毋諱'忠'字，諱而不言，是忘忠也。

translations.literal: Shizhong once admonished his family: "My name is Shizhong; you must not taboo the character 'zhong'; to taboo and not speak it is to forget loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong once warned his family, "My name is Shizhong. You must not avoid the character zhong ('loyalty'). To avoid speaking it is to forget loyalty itself."

sentences.zh: 」性戇直，勇敢忠義，事關廟社，必流涕極言。

translations.literal: His nature was blunt and straight; brave, loyal, and righteous; when matters concerned the altars of state, he always wept and spoke to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he was brave, loyal, and righteous. On matters touching the fate of the realm he wept openly and spoke without restraint.

sentences.zh: 岳飛冤獄，舉朝無敢出一語，世忠獨攖檜怒，語在《檜傳》。

translations.literal: In Yue Fei's unjust imprisonment, the whole court dared not utter a word; Shizhong alone provoked Qin's anger—the account is in the Biography of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei was framed and imprisoned, none at court dared speak out. Shizhong alone provoked Qin Hui's wrath—the full account appears in Qin Hui's biography.

sentences.zh: 又抵排和議，觸檜尤多，或勸止之，世忠曰：「今畏禍苟同，他日瞑目，豈可受鐵杖于太祖殿下？

translations.literal: He also opposed and rejected the peace talks, offending Qin especially often; some urged him to stop; Shizhong said: "Now to fear disaster and go along is easy—but when I close my eyes someday, how could I accept iron rods beneath the Hall of Emperor Taizu?"
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly denounced the peace settlement and offended Qin Hui more than anyone. When some urged caution, Shizhong said, "To fear harm and go along with the crowd is easy—but when I close my eyes, how could I face iron canes beneath the ancestral hall of Emperor Taizu?"

sentences.zh: 」時一二大將，多曲徇檜苟全，世忠與檜同在政地，一揖外未嘗與談。

translations.literal: At that time one or two great generals mostly bent to Qin to preserve themselves; Shizhong and Qin were together in the governing position, but beyond one bow they never conversed.
translations.idiomatic: While other senior generals bent to Qin Hui to save themselves, Shizhong shared office with Qin yet never spoke to him beyond a perfunctory bow.

sentences.zh: 嗜義輕財，錫齎悉分將士，所賜田輸租與編戶等。

translations.literal: He loved righteousness and held wealth lightly; all bestowed gifts he entirely divided among officers and soldiers; for granted fields the rent he paid was equal to common registered households.
translations.idiomatic: He valued honor over wealth and distributed every imperial gift among his troops. For granted estates he paid the same rents as ordinary registered households.

sentences.zh: 持軍嚴重，與士卒同甘苦，器仗規畫，精絕過人，今克敵弓、連鎖甲、狻猊鍪，及跳澗以習騎，洞貫以習射，皆其遺法也。

translations.literal: He held the army with strict dignity, shared bitterness and sweetness with common soldiers; in planning weapons and armor he was surpassingly refined beyond others; today's Enemy-Slaying bow, linked chain armor, lion helmet, and leaping gullies to drill horsemanship, piercing targets to drill archery—all are his legacy methods.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with austere discipline yet shared hardship with his men. His designs for weapons and armor were without equal—the Ke-di bow, linked-ring armor, lion-headed helmets, trench-jumping cavalry drills, and target-piercing archery exercises all survive as his legacy.

sentences.zh: 嘗中毒矢入骨，以強弩括取之，十指僅全四，不能動，刀痕箭瘢如刻畫。

translations.literal: He once took a poisoned arrow into the bone; with a strong crossbow he pried it out; of ten fingers only four remained whole, unable to move; blade marks and arrow scars were like engravings.
translations.idiomatic: A poisoned arrow once lodged in bone. He extracted it with a strong crossbow pull. Only four of his ten fingers remained fully intact and movable; blade cuts and arrow wounds covered him like carved lines.

sentences.zh: 然知人善獎用，成閔、解元、王勝、王權、劉寶、岳超起行伍，秉將旄，皆其部曲雲。

translations.literal: Yet he knew men and was good at encouraging and employing them; Cheng Min, Jie Yuan, Wang Sheng, Wang Quan, Liu Bao, Yue Chao rose from the ranks, held general's banners—all were his personal retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he knew talent and knew how to reward it. Cheng Min, Jie Yuan, Wang Sheng, Wang Quan, Liu Bao, and Yue Chao—all rose from the ranks to hold command under his banner.

sentences.zh: 解兵罷政，臥家凡十年，澹然自如，若未嘗有權位者。

translations.literal: Having relinquished troops and retired from government, he lay at home altogether ten years, tranquil as if he had never held power and position.
translations.idiomatic: After surrendering his army and leaving office he lived at home for ten years, serene as if he had never held power.

sentences.zh: 晚喜釋、老，自號清涼居士。

translations.literal: In his later years he delighted in Buddhism and Daoism and styled himself the Lay Devotee of Pure Coolness.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to Buddhism and Daoism and styled himself the Lay Devotee of Pure Coolness.

sentences.zh: 子彥直、彥質、彥古，皆以才見用。

translations.literal: His sons Yan Zhi, Yan Zhi, and Yan Gu—all were employed for their talent.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yan Zhi, Yan Zhi, and Yan Gu were all employed for their abilities.

sentences.zh: 彥古戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Yan Gu—Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gu served as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子 彥直

translations.literal: Son: Yan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yan Zhi

sentences.zh: 彥直字子溫。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi, style name Ziwen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi, whose style name was Ziwen.

sentences.zh: 生期年，以父任補右承奉郎，尋直秘閣。

translations.literal: When he had lived one full year, through his father's position he was appointed Right Gentleman for Attending Service, and soon was made a member of the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was a year old he was appointed Right Gentleman for Attending Service through his father's rank, and soon entered service at the Secretariat Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 六歲，從世忠入見高宗，命作大字，即拜命跪書「皇帝萬歲」四字。

translations.literal: At six years he followed Shizhong to have an audience with Gaozong, was ordered to write large characters, immediately received the command and knelt to write the four characters "Ten Thousand Years to the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: At six he accompanied Shizhong to an audience with Gaozong, was told to write large characters, and at once knelt to write the four characters "Ten Thousand Years to the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 帝喜之，拊其背曰：「他日，令器也。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with him, patted his back and said: "In the future, a fine vessel indeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, patted his back, and said, "This boy will be a fine vessel one day."

sentences.zh: 」親解孝宗丱角之繻傅其首，賜金器、筆研、監書、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He personally untied the childhood binding cord of Xiaozong and fastened it on his head, and bestowed gold vessels, brush and inkstone, supervised books, and saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He personally untied the childhood binding cord from Xiaozong's head and tied it on the boy's, and gave him gold vessels, writing implements, supervised books, and a saddle and horse.

sentences.zh: 年十二，賜三品服。

translations.literal: At twelve years he was granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was granted robes of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，遷戶部郎官、主管左曹，總領淮東軍馬錢糧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he was transferred to Lang official of the Revenue Ministry, supervised the Left Bureau, and oversaw overall Huaidong army funds, horses, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qiandao reign he was made a Lang official of the Revenue Ministry, placed in charge of the Left Bureau, and put in overall charge of Huaidong army funds, horses, and grain.

sentences.zh: 會大軍倉給糧，徑乘小輿往察之，給米不如數，捕吏寘於理。

translations.literal: It happened the great army granary was issuing grain; he went straight in a small carriage to inspect it; the rice issued did not match the count, and he arrested the clerk and placed him before the law.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army granary was issuing rations he went in person in a small carriage to inspect it. Finding the rice short of the proper amount, he arrested the clerk and brought him to justice.

sentences.zh: 初，代者以乏興罷，交承，為緡錢僅二十萬，明年奏計乃四倍，且以其贏獻諸朝。

translations.literal: At first his predecessor had been dismissed for lack of funds; on handover there were only two hundred thousand strings of cash; the next year when accounts were submitted it was fourfold, and moreover he presented the surplus to court.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had been dismissed for short funds, leaving only two hundred thousand strings of cash on handover. The next year Yan Zhi's accounts showed four times that amount, and he presented the surplus to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 拜司農少卿，進直龍圖閣、江西轉運兼權知江州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Agriculture, advanced to direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and made Jiangxi transport commissioner with acting authority over Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Agriculture, made a direct attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and named Jiangxi transport commissioner with acting authority over Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷還岳飛家貲產多在九江，歲久業數易主，吏緣為奸。

translations.literal: At that time the court was restoring Yue Fei's family property, much of which lay in Jiujiang; over the years estates had changed hands many times, and clerks took advantage to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then restoring Yue Fei's family property, much of it in Jiujiang. Over the years the estates had changed hands repeatedly, and officials used this to commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 彥直搜剔隱匿，盡還岳氏。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi searched out concealed holdings and returned everything to the Yue clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi tracked down concealed holdings and restored everything to the Yue family.

sentences.zh: 復為司農少卿，總領湖北、京西軍馬錢糧，尋兼發運副使。

translations.literal: He again became Vice Minister of Agriculture, oversaw overall Hubei and Jingxi army funds, horses, and grain, and soon also served as deputy transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Vice Minister of Agriculture and took overall charge of Hubei and Jingxi army funds, horses, and grain, soon adding the post of deputy transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會時相不樂，密啟換武，授利州觀察使、知襄陽府，充京西南路安撫使。

translations.literal: It happened the chief minister was displeased and secretly memorialized to transfer him to military service; he was appointed observation commissioner of Li Prefecture, prefect of Xiangyang, and filled the post of pacification commissioner for southwestern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister took a dislike to him and secretly had him transferred to military service. He was appointed observation commissioner of Li Prefecture, prefect of Xiangyang, and pacification commissioner for southwestern Jing.

sentences.zh: 七年，授鄂州駐劄御前諸軍都統制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed overall commander of all armies stationed before the throne at Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed overall commander of all imperial armies stationed at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 條奏軍中六事，乞備器械、增戰馬、革濫賞、厲奇功、選勇略、充親隨等，朝廷多從之。

translations.literal: He itemized six matters in the army and memorialized, begging to prepare weapons, increase war horses, reform excessive rewards, encourage extraordinary merit, select courage and strategy, fill personal followers, and the like; the court largely followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on six army reforms: stock weapons, increase war horses, curb excessive rewards, encourage extraordinary merit, select men of courage and strategy, and fill personal staffs. The court largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 先是，軍中騎兵多不能步戰，彥直命騎士被甲徒行，日六十里，雖統制官亦令以身帥之，人人習於勞苦，馳騁如飛。

translations.literal: Earlier, army cavalry mostly could not fight on foot; Yan Zhi ordered horsemen to wear armor and march on foot sixty li a day; even commanders were made to lead by example in person; every man grew accustomed to hardship, and when they galloped it was like flight.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry in the army had largely been unable to fight on foot. Yan Zhi ordered horsemen to march in armor sixty li a day; even commanders had to lead by example. The men grew hardened to hardship and rode like the wind.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔令三衙、江上諸軍仿行之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the Three Commands and all armies along the Yangtze to imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, the court ordered the Three Commands and all Yangtze armies to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 八年，丐歸文班，乃授左中奉大夫，充敷文閣待制、知台州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he begged to return to the civil roster; he was then appointed Left Grand Master for Attending Service, made a drafting attendant of the Fuwen Hall, and prefect of Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he asked to return to civil office and was appointed Left Grand Master for Attending Service, drafting attendant of the Fuwen Hall, and prefect of Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丐祠養親，提舉佑神觀、奉朝請。

translations.literal: He begged a temple post to support his parents, was made director of the You Shen Abbey and court attendee.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a temple post to care for his parents and was made director of the You Shen Abbey with the rank of court attendee.

sentences.zh: 進對言：「頃自岳飛為帥，身居鄂渚，遙領荊襄，田師中繼之，始分鄂渚為二軍，乞復舊。

translations.literal: In an audience he said: "Recently, since Yue Fei was commander, he dwelt at Ezhou and remotely led Jing and Xiang; Tian Shizhong succeeded him and only then divided Ezhou into two armies—I beg to restore the old arrangement."
translations.idiomatic: At court he said, "When Yue Fei commanded, he was based at Ezhou and held Jing and Xiang from afar. Tian Shizhong later split Ezhou into two armies. I ask that the old arrangement be restored."

sentences.zh: 」又乞並京西、湖北轉運為一司，分官置司襄陽，可一事體，帝善之。

translations.literal: He also begged to merge Jingxi and Hubei transport into one office, with separate officials establishing headquarters at Xiangyang, so that affairs could be handled as one body; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to merge the Jingxi and Hubei transport offices into one, with a branch at Xiangyang, so the region could be managed as a single unit. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼工部侍郎，同列議：大辟三鞫之弗承，宜令以眾證就刑，欲修立為令。

translations.literal: The next year, while also Vice Minister of Works, his colleagues debated: for capital cases tried three times without confession, they should be made to suffer execution on collective evidence, and wished to establish this as statute.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, while also serving as Vice Minister of Works, his colleagues proposed that when a capital defendant refused to confess after three interrogations, he should be executed on collective evidence alone, and they wished to codify this as law.

sentences.zh: 彥直持不可，白丞相梁克家曰：「若是，則善類被誣，必多冤獄。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi held it could not be done and told Chief Councillor Liang Kejia: "If so, then good people will be slandered and wrongful cases will surely multiply."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi objected and told Chief Councillor Liang Kejia, "If we do this, good men will be framed and wrongful convictions will multiply."

sentences.zh: 且笞杖之刑，猶引伏方決，況人命至重乎？

translations.literal: Moreover for flogging punishments one still waits for confession before deciding—how much more when human life is utmost in weight?"
translations.idiomatic: Even for flogging one waits for a confession before sentencing. How much more so when a human life is at stake?"

sentences.zh: 」議卒格。

translations.literal: The proposal in the end was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was blocked.

sentences.zh: 以議奪吳名世改正過名不當，降兩官。

translations.literal: For debating he was judged to have improperly seized Wu Mingshi's correction of an erroneous name and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted two ranks on a charge arising from a dispute over correcting Wu Mingshi's name in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 會當遣使于金，在廷相顧莫肯先，帝親擇以往，聞命慨然就道。

translations.literal: It happened an envoy was to be sent to the Jin; at court all looked at one another and none would go first; the emperor personally chose him to go; hearing the command he set out on the road with deep feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy was needed to the Jin, no one at court would volunteer. The emperor chose Yan Zhi himself, and on receiving the order he set out resolutely.

sentences.zh: 方入境，金使蒲察問接國書事，論難往復數十，蒲察理屈，因笑曰：「尚書能力為主。

translations.literal: Just as he entered the border, the Jin envoy Pucha asked about receiving the state letter; argument went back and forth several tens of times; Pucha was defeated in reason, and therefore laughed, saying: "The Vice Minister is able to serve his sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Just inside the border the Jin envoy Pucha questioned him about receiving the state letter. After dozens of exchanges Pucha was left without an answer and laughed, "The Vice Minister serves his sovereign well."

sentences.zh: 」既至，幾罹禍者數，守節不屈，金卒禮遣之，帝嘉歎。

translations.literal: After arriving, several times he nearly suffered disaster, held to his integrity without yielding, and the Jin in the end sent him off with ceremony; the emperor praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he nearly came to harm several times but held firm. The Jin finally sent him off with ceremony. The emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，尋權工部尚書，復中大夫，改工部尚書兼知臨安府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, soon acted as Minister of Works, was restored to Grand Master for Attending Service, and changed to Minister of Works with concurrent prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Personnel, then acting Minister of Works, restored to Grand Master for Attending Service, and appointed Minister of Works with concurrent prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 方控辭，以言罷，提舉太平興國宮，尋提舉佑神觀、奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was just declining the post when because of his words he was dismissed, made director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, and soon director of the You Shen Abbey and court attendee.
translations.idiomatic: He was declining the post when remarks he made cost him the office. He was made director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, then director of the You Shen Abbey with the rank of court attendee.

sentences.zh: 尋知濕州，首捕巨猾王永年窮治之，杖徙他州。

translations.literal: Soon he was prefect of Wen Prefecture; first he captured the great villain Wang Yongnian and prosecuted him to the end, flogged and exiled to another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Wen Prefecture. He captured the notorious criminal Wang Yongnian, prosecuted him thoroughly, and had him flogged and exiled to another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奏免民間積逋，以郡餘財代輸之，然以累欠內帑坊場錢不發，鐫一官。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit accumulated arrears owed by the people, using surplus prefectural funds to pay on their behalf; however because he had long failed to issue inner-palace workshop monies he was cut one rank.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to remit accumulated tax arrears, paying them from prefectural surplus funds, but was demoted one rank for long failing to remit inner-palace workshop revenues.

sentences.zh: 海寇出沒大洋劫掠，勢甚張，彥直授將領土豪等方略，不旬日，生禽賊首，海道為清。

translations.literal: Sea bandits appeared and vanished on the great ocean plundering, their momentum very strong; Yan Zhi gave generals, local strongmen, and others strategy; within ten days the bandit chief was captured alive and the sea routes were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Sea pirates were raiding boldly on the open ocean. Yan Zhi gave his generals and local leaders a plan, and within ten days the pirate chief was captured alive and the sea lanes were cleared.

sentences.zh: 樞密奏功，進敷文閣學士，以弟彥質為兩浙轉運判官，引嫌易泉府。

translations.literal: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported his merit; he was advanced to academician of the Fuwen Hall; because his younger brother Yan Zhi was transport judge of the two Zhe circuits, he cited conflict of interest and was moved to Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs reported his achievement and he was promoted to academician of the Fuwen Hall. Because his brother Yan Zhi was transport judge of the two Zhe circuits, he cited conflict of interest and was transferred to Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丐祠奉親，差提舉佑神觀，仍奉朝請，特令佩魚，示異數也。

translations.literal: He begged a temple post to support his parents, was assigned director of the You Shen Abbey, still court attendee, and specially ordered to wear the fish tally, showing special favor.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a temple post to care for his parents and was assigned director of the You Shen Abbey while retaining court attendee rank. He was specially granted the fish tally, a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 入對，乞搜訪靖康以來死節之士，以勸忠義。

translations.literal: In an audience he begged to search out men who had died for integrity since Jingkang, to encourage loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked that men who had died for their integrity since the Jingkang disaster be sought out and honored, to encourage loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又上薦舉乞選人已經關升、實曆六考、無贓私罪犯者，雜試以經術法律，限其員額，定其高下，俾孤寒者得以自達，定為改官之制。

translations.literal: He also submitted recommendations begging that candidates who had passed the barrier promotion, served six actual examinations, and had no corruption or private crimes be tested in mixed examinations on classics and law, with limits on quotas and determination of rank high and low, so that the isolated and poor could advance themselves, establishing this as the system for changing office.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that candidates who had passed promotion barriers, completed six examinations in service, and had no corruption convictions be tested in classics and law, with fixed quotas and ranks, so that men of humble origin could advance. This became the system for civil promotion.

sentences.zh: 又乞令州郡守臣任滿日，開具本州實在財賦數目，具公移與交代者，並達台省，庶可核實，以戢奸弊，帝悉嘉納。

translations.literal: He also begged that on the day prefectural and commandery守 officials completed their terms they should open and list the actual revenue and tax figures of the prefecture, provide official documents to their successors, and reach both the provincial commission and central ministries, so that verification could be made and fraud curbed; the emperor fully praised and adopted all.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that when prefects completed their terms they submit a full accounting of the prefecture's actual revenues to their successors and to the provincial and central authorities, so accounts could be verified and fraud curbed. The emperor approved all these proposals.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年夏旱，應詔言，邇者濫刑，為致旱之由。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunxi there was summer drought; responding to an edict he said that recently excessive punishments were the cause bringing drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Chunxi reign a summer drought struck. Responding to an imperial edict he said that excessive punishments of late were the cause of the drought.

sentences.zh: 明年，入對，論三衙皆所以拱扈宸居，而司馬乃遠在數百里外，乞令歸司。

translations.literal: The next year, in an audience, he discussed that the Three Commands all exist to guard and escort the imperial residence, yet the marshal is far off several hundred li away, and begged to order him back to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The next year at court he argued that the Three Commands exist to guard the imperial residence, yet their marshal was stationed hundreds of li away, and asked that he be ordered back to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 久之，再為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he again became Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he again became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，乞廣糴為先備。

translations.literal: It happened the year was drought-stricken; he begged to purchase grain widely as prior preparation.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck again he asked that grain be purchased widely as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 又乞追貶部曲曾誣陷岳飛者，以慰忠魂。

translations.literal: He also begged to pursue posthumous demotion of subordinates who had once framed Yue Fei, to comfort the loyal soul.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that subordinates who had once framed Yue Fei be posthumously demoted, to comfort Yue's loyal spirit.

sentences.zh: 以言降充敷文閣學士。

translations.literal: Because of his words he was demoted to academician of the Fuwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His remarks cost him a demotion to academician of the Fuwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝追感世忠元勳，遣使諭彥直，且謂彥直有才力，言者誣之。

translations.literal: The emperor, recalling Shizhong's founding merit with emotion, sent an envoy to instruct Yan Zhi, and moreover said Yan Zhi had talent and ability and that critics had slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by memory of Shizhong's founding service, sent an envoy to reassure Yan Zhi, saying he had talent and that his critics had slandered him.

sentences.zh: 彥直感泣奏謝。

translations.literal: Yan Zhi, moved to tears, memorialized thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhi wept as he memorialized his thanks.

sentences.zh: 尋提舉萬壽觀，有疾，帝賜之藥。

translations.literal: Soon he was director of the Wanshou Abbey; he had illness and the emperor bestowed medicine on him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the Wanshou Abbey. When he fell ill the emperor sent him medicine.

sentences.zh: 進顯謨閣學士、提舉萬壽觀。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Xianmo Hall and director of the Wanshou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Xianmo Hall and director of the Wanshou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 嘗摭宋朝事，分為類目，名《水心鏡》，為書百六十七卷。

translations.literal: He once gathered Song affairs, divided them into categories, named it Mirror of the Water Heart, and made a book of one hundred sixty-seven scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled Song history by category into a work of one hundred sixty-seven scrolls called Mirror of the Water Heart.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書尤袤修國史，白於朝，下取是書以進，光宗覽之，稱善。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites You Mao was revising the national history, reported to court, ordered this book taken and presented, and Guangzong perused it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Rites You Mao was revising the national history he reported to court, had the book submitted, and Guangzong read it with approval.

sentences.zh: 進龍圖閣學士、提舉萬壽觀，轉光祿大夫致仕。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Wanshou Abbey, and transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and director of the Wanshou Abbey, then retired as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，特贈開府儀同三司，賜銀絹九百，爵至蘄春郡公。

translations.literal: He died; specially posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, bestowed nine hundred of silver and silk, and ennobled to Duke of Qichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, given nine hundred measures of silver and silk, and ennobled as Duke of Qichun.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人有言：「天下安，注意相；

translations.literal: The commentary says: The ancients had a saying: "When the realm is secure, attend to the chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The ancients observed, "When the realm is at peace, look to the chancellor;

sentences.zh: 天下危，注意將。

translations.literal: when the realm is in peril, attend to the general."
translations.idiomatic: when the realm is in peril, look to the general."

sentences.zh: 」宋靖康、建炎之際，天下安危之機也，勇略忠義如韓世忠而為將，是天以資宋之興復也。

translations.literal: At the time of Song's Jingkang and Jianyan, it was the pivot of the realm's security and peril; for one of courage, strategy, loyalty, and righteousness like Han Shizhong to be general was heaven supplying Song's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingkang and Jianyan crises the fate of the realm hung in the balance. That a man of courage, strategy, loyalty, and righteousness like Han Shizhong should serve as general was heaven's gift to the Song restoration.

sentences.zh: 方兀朮渡江，惟世忠與之對陣，以閒暇示之。

translations.literal: When Wuzhu crossed the Yangtze, only Shizhong faced him in battle array and showed him leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhu crossed the Yangtze, Shizhong alone faced him in battle and met him with apparent ease.

sentences.zh: 及劉豫廢，中原人心動搖，世忠請乘時進兵，此機何可失也？

translations.literal: When Liu Yu was deposed, hearts in the central plains were shaken; Shizhong requested to seize the time and advance troops—how could such an opportunity be lost?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu was deposed and hearts in the Central Plains wavered, Shizhong urged an advance. What opportunity could be more precious?

sentences.zh: 高宗惟奸檜之言是聽，使世忠不得盡展其才，和議成而宋事去矣。

translations.literal: Gaozong only listened to the words of the traitor Hui, so that Shizhong could not fully display his talent; the peace agreement was made and Song's cause was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong listened only to the traitor Qin Hui, so Shizhong could never fully deploy his gifts. The peace treaty was made, and the Song cause was lost.

sentences.zh: 暮年退居行都，口不言兵，部曲舊將，不與相見，蓋懲岳飛之事也。

translations.literal: In his late years he retired to dwell in the traveling capital, never spoke of war, and did not meet his old commanders and generals—probably warning himself by Yue Fei's affair.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived in retirement at the traveling capital, never spoke of war, and would not see his former officers—no doubt mindful of what had befallen Yue Fei.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝思頗、牧於前代，宋有世忠而不善用，惜哉！

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han thought of Po and Mu from earlier ages; Song had Shizhong yet did not employ him well—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han once longed for generals like Lian Po and Li Mu from ages past. The Song had Han Shizhong and did not use him well. What a pity!
